classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field
items.description:
Poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic field is the poloidal component of the
complex linear-MHD eigenfunction, or corresponding real perturbation, of the
magnetic-field deviation carried by the confined-plasma response about
equilibrium.
items.documentation:
Poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic field is the poloidal component of the
complex linear-MHD eigenfunction, or corresponding real perturbation, of the
magnetic-field deviation carried by the confined-plasma response about an
equilibrium magnetic field. It is the poloidal projection of the [perturbed
plasma magnetic field](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field), rather than
the unrestricted magnetic-field vector.

$$
\delta B_{\mathrm{pol}}(\mathbf{x},t)=\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{pol}}(\mathbf{x})\cdot\delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pl}}(\mathbf{x},t)
$$

Here, $\delta B_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal component, $\hat{\mathbf
e}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the chosen poloidal unit vector in the poloidal plane
of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and
$\delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the plasma-response perturbation after
subtracting the equilibrium field and any separately represented externally
imposed vacuum perturbation. The complex quantity includes the [poloidal
real part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part) and
[poloidal imaginary
part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part); the
[toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic
field](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field) is its complementary
toroidal projection.

Sign convention: Positive when the perturbed magnetic field points in the
direction of increasing poloidal angle within the poloidal plane of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: electron_density_at_pellet_path
items.description:
Local free-electron number density of the background plasma at points along
a pellet's ablation trajectory.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the local number density of free electrons in the background
plasma at each point traversed by an injected pellet. It describes the
plasma encountered by the pellet, not electron content in pellet material or
electron production by ablation.

At a path point, the electron number density is defined by the local
number-to-volume ratio:

$$
n_e = \lim_{\Delta V \to 0} \frac{\Delta N_e}{\Delta V}
$$

where $n_e$ is the electron number density, $\Delta N_e$ is the number of
free electrons in the volume element $\Delta V$, and $\Delta V$ is the
volume element centered at the path point.

The quantity is evaluated locally along the pellet trajectory and is
distinct from the [electron source rate at the pellet path due to pellet
injection](name:electron_source_rate_at_pellet_path_due_to_pellet_injection),
which describes electron production rather than background density. It has
the same physical meaning as [electron density at the launching
position](name:electron_density_at_launching_position), but at a different
locus.

items.name: poloidal_plane_cross_sectional_area_of_flux_surface
items.description:
Area enclosed by a magnetic flux-surface contour in a poloidal plane at
fixed toroidal angle, including the complete planar interior.
items.documentation:
Area of flux surface

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the enclosed area is
defined by

$$
A_{\mathrm{p}} = \iint_{\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{p}}} dR\,dZ
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal-plane cross-sectional area,
$\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the planar region enclosed by the selected
contour, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical
height, and $dR\,dZ$ is the unsigned poloidal-plane area element.

This quantity applies to any selected closed flux-surface contour and
includes its entire interior, not merely the region between neighboring
contours. It is not a local area element, a flux-surface average, or the
[surface area of the flux surface](name:surface_area_of_flux_surface), which
covers its full poloidal and toroidal extent.

At the plasma boundary, it becomes the [poloidal-plane cross-sectional area
of the plasma
boundary](name:poloidal_plane_cross_sectional_area_of_plasma_boundary). Its
local variation between neighboring surfaces is described by the [derivative
with respect to poloidal magnetic flux
coordinate](name:derivative_of_poloidal_plane_cross_sectional_area_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_poloidal_magnetic_flux_coordinate)
or the [derivative with respect to toroidal flux
coordinate](name:derivative_of_poloidal_plane_cross_sectional_area_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_toroidal_flux_coordinate),
according to the coordinate used.

A surface formed by points sharing the same magnetic-flux label in a
nested-flux-surface configuration. Where $\psi(R, Z) = \mathrm{const}$,
$\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux.

items.name: co_passing_fast_particle_pressure
items.description:
Co-passing fast-particle pressure is one-third of the kinetic-stress trace
carried by suprathermal particles on untrapped orbits whose orbit-averaged
toroidal motion is in the same direction as the plasma current. It sums
contributions over fast-particle species and charge states and retains
directed-motion stress.
items.documentation:
Co-passing fast-particle pressure is one-third of the kinetic-stress trace
carried by the suprathermal particles on untrapped co-passing orbits. These
orbits have orbit-averaged toroidal motion in the same direction as the
plasma current; the scalar trace includes field-aligned, transverse, and
directed-motion contributions without requiring an isotropic velocity
distribution.

The pressure is defined by the second velocity moment restricted to the
co-passing region:

$$
P_{\mathrm{co,fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{1}{3}\sum_s\sum_c m_s\int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{co},s,c}(\mathbf{x})} |\mathbf{v}|^2 f_{s,c,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{co,fast}}$ is the co-passing fast-particle pressure,
$\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, $s$ labels fast-particle species, $c$
labels charge state, $m_s$ is the mass of species $s$, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, $f_{s,c,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the suprathermal distribution
function for species $s$ and charge state $c$,
$\Omega_{\mathrm{co},s,c}(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space region of
untrapped co-passing particles at position $\mathbf{x}$, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element. The distribution includes represented
fast-particle populations additively, and the velocity is not centered on
the selected population's mean, so directed-motion stress is retained.

The quantity applies to the suprathermal co-passing population only.
Contributions are summed over all fast-particle species and charge states;
thermal particles and the counter-passing and trapped orbit classes are
excluded. The pressure is defined locally, and its flux-surface-averaged
form averages this same local quantity over a magnetic flux surface without
changing the orbit-class selection.

The trace combines the [parallel co-passing fast-particle
pressure](name:parallel_co_passing_fast_particle_pressure) and the
[perpendicular co-passing fast-particle
pressure](name:perpendicular_co_passing_fast_particle_pressure):
$P_{\mathrm{co,fast}}=(P_{\parallel,\mathrm{co,fast}}+2P_{\perp,\mathrm{co,fast}})/3$,
where $P_{\parallel,\mathrm{co,fast}}$ is the field-aligned kinetic stress
and $P_{\perp,\mathrm{co,fast}}$ is the mean stress per transverse direction
for the same population. This orbit-selected contribution is part of
[fast-particle pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure), not the all-orbit
fast-particle pressure itself.

items.name: current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive
items.description:
Net toroidal plasma current generated non-inductively by wave–particle
interactions, including cumulative and toroidal-mode-resolved
representations.
items.documentation:
Wave-driven current is the toroidal plasma current attributable to momentum
transfer from externally applied electromagnetic waves through wave–particle
interactions. It excludes inductive current and non-wave non-inductive
current sources.

For a selected poloidal cross-sectional area, the current is defined by

$$
I_{\mathrm{wd}} = \int_A j_{\mathrm{wd},\phi}(R,Z)\,dA
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{wd}}$ is the wave-driven current, $A$ is the selected
poloidal area, $j_{\mathrm{wd},\phi}$ is the toroidal component of the
wave-driven current density, and $(R,\phi,Z)$ is the right-handed
cylindrical frame. For a flux-surface-enclosed area, this gives the
cumulative quantity represented by [toroidal current due to wave-driven
current drive](name:toroidal_current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive); the
same current may be decomposed into per-toroidal-mode current.

Sign convention: Positive when the wave-driven plasma current flows in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: radial_wave_electric_field
items.description:
Complex phasor of the wave electric field projected onto the R direction of
the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, preserving local amplitude,
phase, and radial polarization.
items.documentation:
The radial wave electric field is the complex phasor obtained by projecting
the electromagnetic-wave electric-field phasor onto the cylindrical
major-radius direction. It is a component of the [wave electric
field](name:wave_electric_field) and retains the local wave amplitude and
phase.

For a wave with angular frequency $\omega$, the radial phasor is defined by

$$
\widetilde{E}_r(\mathbf{r},\omega)=\widetilde{\mathbf{E}}_{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r},\omega)\cdot\hat{R}
$$

where $\widetilde{\mathbf{E}}_{\mathrm{wave}}$ is the complex
wave-electric-field phasor, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $\hat{R}$ is the
major-radius unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.
Unlike the [normal wave electric field](name:normal_wave_electric_field),
this component follows the cylindrical $R$ direction and is not a projection
normal to a magnetic flux surface. It complements the [vertical wave
electric field](name:vertical_wave_electric_field) in describing cylindrical
polarization.

Sign convention: Positive when the corresponding electric-field component
points toward increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: safety_factor_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Signed field-line winding ratio evaluated on the magnetic flux surface
designated as the internal transport barrier, giving toroidal turns per
poloidal circuit.
items.documentation:
The safety factor at the internal transport barrier is the signed helical
winding of magnetic field lines on the flux surface designated as the
barrier. It counts toroidal turns per poloidal circuit at that specific
locus.

The defining flux-increment relation is:

$$
q_{\mathrm{ITB}} = \left.\frac{d\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}}{d\Phi_{\mathrm{pol}}}\right|_{\mathrm{ITB}}
$$

where $q_{\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the safety factor evaluated on the
internal-transport-barrier flux surface, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is toroidal
magnetic flux, $\Phi_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is poloidal magnetic flux, and the
subscript $\mathrm{ITB}$ denotes evaluation on that designated surface.

This quantity applies only to the flux surface associated with the internal
transport barrier. It is a single flux-surface value, with no averaging or
aggregation over neighboring surfaces, plasma volume, or other regions
implied.

It is distinct from safety-factor values evaluated at other loci, such as
the safety factor at the pedestal top, and it does not represent a general
radial profile or a value at the magnetic axis or plasma boundary.

The [safety factor](name:safety_factor) is the corresponding
locus-independent flux-surface quantity; this name specializes it by fixing
the evaluation surface. The [rotational
transform](name:rotational_transform) uses the reciprocal field-line winding
convention, counting poloidal turns per toroidal circuit.

Sign convention: Positive when the toroidal and poloidal flux increments
have the same sign, taking $\phi$ as the toroidal angle in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major radius, $Z$ the vertical
height, and the positive poloidal circuit defined by increasing
$\Phi_{\mathrm{pol}}$.

items.name: trapped_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force
items.description:
Angular-momentum source per unit volume generated by the Lorentz force,
averaged over a magnetic flux surface for trapped particles.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged torque density transferred to
trapped particles by the magnetic Lorentz force associated with their
current contribution. Trapped particles are the orbit population whose
guiding-center parallel motion is confined between magnetic-mirror bounce
points rather than circulating as a passing orbit.

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{J\times B}^{\mathrm{tr}}(\psi)=\left\langle\mathbf{r}\times\left(\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{tr}}\times\mathbf{B}\right)\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{J\times B}^{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the torque-density
vector, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the selected torque origin,
$\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the current-density contribution associated
with trapped particles, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, and $\psi$
labels the magnetic flux surface. The angle brackets denote a flux-surface
average.

This orbit-resolved vector is a member of the [torque density due to J×B
force](name:torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) family. Its toroidal
projection is represented by [toroidal trapped torque density due to J×B
force](name:toroidal_trapped_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force).
Passing-orbit quantities such as [co-passing torque density due to J×B
force](name:co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) and
[counter-passing torque density due to J×B
force](name:counter_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) describe
different orbit populations and are not specializations of this trapped
quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved torque component points in the
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame.

items.name: reflected_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
items.description:
Relative phase angle of a reflected radio-frequency power-wave phasor at an
antenna element in an ion-cyclotron heating launcher, measured relative to
the forward power-wave phasor of that same element.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the relative phase of a complex reflected radio-frequency
power-wave phasor at a selected antenna strap or module with respect to the
complex forward radio-frequency power-wave phasor of the same strap or
module. It specifies the element-local reflection phase of an ion-cyclotron
heating launcher rather than an absolute phase or an inter-element phase.

For element $i$, the reflected phase is defined by

$$
\phi_{\mathrm{ref},i} = \arg\!\left(b_i^{\mathrm{ref}} (a_i^{\mathrm{fwd}})^*\right) \pmod{2\pi}
$$

where $\phi_{\mathrm{ref},i}$ is this reflected phase, $b_i^{\mathrm{ref}}$
is the complex reflected power-wave phasor at element $i$,
$a_i^{\mathrm{fwd}}$ is the complex forward power-wave phasor at the same
element, $(a_i^{\mathrm{fwd}})^*$ is its complex conjugate, and $\arg$
extracts the phase angle. The phase is defined modulo $2\pi$.

The scope is a single selected launcher strap or module and the pair of
forward and reflected traveling power waves at the same element reference
plane. The forward wave propagates toward the antenna element, and the
reflected wave propagates away from the antenna element toward the feeding
network. The first launcher element is not the phase reference for this
quantity, and the quantity is not averaged or summed over launcher elements.

This quantity is a reflected-wave member of the broader phase of the
ion-cyclotron heating antenna family. It is distinct from the [wave phase of
the ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), which describes
inter-element phasing, and together with the [reflected power of the
ion-cyclotron heating
antenna](name:reflected_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) it specifies
the phase-and-magnitude state of the reflected power wave without including
the magnitude itself.

Sign convention: Positive when the reflected-wave phasor at the selected
element leads the forward-wave phasor at the same element in phase under the
adopted temporal phasor convention.

items.name: derivative_of_logarithm_of_density_with_respect_to_normalized_minor_radius
items.description:
Signed logarithmic derivative of a selected particle-species density with
respect to normalized minor radius, expressing the relative change of that
density as the normalized minor-radius coordinate increases. For
charge-state-aggregated ion species, the density is summed over all charge
states.
items.documentation:
Signed logarithmic derivative of a selected particle-species density with
respect to normalized minor radius is the local derivative of that species
density's natural logarithm along the normalized minor-radius coordinate. It
represents the relative change of the selected species density with respect
to that coordinate.

The derivative is defined by

$$
G_{n_s} = \frac{\partial \ln n_s}{\partial \rho} = \frac{1}{n_s}\frac{\partial n_s}{\partial \rho}
$$

where $G_{n_s}$ is this logarithmic derivative, $n_s$ is the density of the
selected particle species $s$, and $\rho$ is the normalized minor radius,
the radial coordinate in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$
increasing from the magnetic axis toward the plasma boundary.

The scope is one selected particle species at the position where the
derivative is evaluated. When the selected species represents a
charge-state-aggregated ion population, $n_s$ is the charge-state-summed
density over all charge states; it is not a density-weighted charge-state
mean and not a total over unrelated species.

This quantity is the derivative of the logarithmic density with respect to
$\rho$, not the density itself, not the logarithm alone, and not a
coordinate-specialized value of a logarithm-of-density quantity.
Logarithmic-gradient conventions that add an extra minus sign or
differentiate with respect to an unnormalized minor-radius coordinate denote
different quantities.

Sign convention: Positive when $\ln n_s$ increases with increasing
normalized minor-radius coordinate $\rho$.

items.name: normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density
items.description:
Dimensionless vector of the charge-weighted first velocity moment of a
perturbed gyrocenter distribution, scaled by a positive reference
current-density magnitude.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the normalized perturbed gyrocenter current-density vector:
the charge-weighted first velocity moment of a perturbed gyrocenter
distribution. It represents the vector current response, distinct from
density and pressure moments.

The charge-weighted moment and its normalization are defined by

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{gc}}^{\delta}=\sum_s q_s\int \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{gc}}\,\delta f_{\mathrm{gc},s}\,d^3\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{gc}},\qquad \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{gc}}^{\delta}=\frac{\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{gc}}^{\delta}}{J_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $q_s$ is the charge of species $s$, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{gc}}$ is
gyrocenter velocity, $\delta f_{\mathrm{gc},s}$ is the perturbed gyrocenter
distribution, and $J_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference
current-density scale. The vector may be resolved into directional
projections; [parallel normalized gyrocenter perturbed current
density](name:parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density) is
one such field-aligned component. The [normalized gyrocenter perturbed
density](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_density) is the corresponding
zeroth moment, while normalized gyrocenter perturbed pressure is a second
moment.

Sign convention: Positive when a projected component of the charge-weighted
perturbed gyrocenter flow points along its assigned positive basis
direction.

items.name: boron_density_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Boron density at the divertor target is the local number density of boron
ions immediately upstream of the electrostatic sheath at the target-facing
plasma boundary.
items.documentation:
Boron density at the divertor target is the local number density of boron
ions in the plasma immediately adjacent to the divertor target surface,
evaluated at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath. It is the
boron-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The charge-state-summed boron ion density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{B}} = \sum_{q=1}^{5} n_{\mathrm{B}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{B}}$ is the boron ion number density and
$n_{\mathrm{B}^{q+}}$ is the number density of boron ions with positive
charge state $q$.

This quantity applies to the boron-ion population immediately upstream of
the sheath at a divertor target and aggregates all positive boron ionization
states, from singly ionized through fully stripped boron. Each boron ion is
counted once; neutral boron atoms are excluded.

Relative to the parent
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target), this quantity
selects boron ions rather than an unspecified species or species group. It
is parallel to
[beryllium_density_at_divertor_target](name:beryllium_density_at_divertor_target),
differing in the selected ion species and its allowed charge states.

items.name: neutral_torque_density
items.description:
Net angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume from neutral particles to
the plasma, summed over all neutral internal states and retaining the
complete torque-vector direction.
items.documentation:
Torque density for neutral particles is the net angular-momentum transfer
rate to the plasma per unit volume produced by neutral–plasma momentum
exchange, summed over all neutral internal states. It retains the complete
torque-vector direction rather than selecting a toroidal component or a
particular neutral state.

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{n\to p} = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0} \frac{1}{\Delta V}\frac{d\boldsymbol{L}_{p\leftarrow n}}{dt}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{n\to p}$ is the torque-density vector transferred
from neutrals to the plasma, $\boldsymbol{L}_{p\leftarrow n}$ is the
corresponding angular momentum transferred to the plasma, $\Delta V$ is a
volume element, and $t$ is time.

This is the neutral-exchange contribution to the broader [torque
density](name:torque_density); it excludes source terms unrelated to
neutral–plasma momentum exchange. The [toroidal neutral torque
density](name:toroidal_neutral_torque_density) is its toroidal component.

Sign convention: Positive when each resolved component points along the
corresponding positive unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical
$(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ basis, with
$\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$.

items.name: minor_length_of_plasma_filament
items.description:
Length of the minor oblique parallelogram side of a plasma-filament element,
inclined at angle beta to the vertical height axis.
items.documentation:
The minor oblique parallelogram-side length of a plasma-filament element is
the Euclidean length of the side inclined at angle beta to the vertical
height direction. It characterizes one side of the element's oblique
cross-sectional geometry.

The side length is defined by the separation of its two endpoints:

$$
\ell_\beta = \left\lVert \mathbf{x}_{\beta,2} - \mathbf{x}_{\beta,1} \right\rVert
$$

where $\ell_\beta$ is the minor side length, $\mathbf{x}_{\beta,1}$ and
$\mathbf{x}_{\beta,2}$ are the position vectors of its endpoints, and
$\lVert\cdot\rVert$ denotes the Euclidean norm. The inclination angle
$\beta$ is measured relative to the vertical height direction in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity applies to one discrete plasma current-carrying filament
element and is neither summed nor averaged over elements. It excludes the
complementary major oblique side and therefore is distinct from [major
length of the plasma filament](name:major_length_of_plasma_filament).

This quantity specializes length of the plasma filament by selecting its
minor, beta-inclined side. The paired major-length quantity selects the
complementary oblique side of the same element.

items.name: toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density
items.description:
Toroidal angular-momentum source rate per unit volume from counter-passing
particles, obtained by applying the major-radius lever arm to their net
toroidal force density.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local toroidal angular-momentum source rate per unit
volume associated with counter-passing particles. Counter-passing particles
have guiding-center parallel motion opposite to the plasma-current
direction.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the toroidal torque
density is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{cp}}(R,\phi,Z)=R\,f_{\phi}^{\mathrm{cp}}(R,\phi,Z)
$$

where $\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the counter-passing toroidal torque
density, $R$ is the major-radius lever arm, and $f_{\phi}^{\mathrm{cp}}$ is
the net toroidal force density on the counter-passing population. The force
density is summed over the included particle species and momentum-exchange
mechanisms.

This is the toroidal component of counter_passing_torque_density,
distinguished from the co-passing contribution represented by
[toroidal_co_passing_torque_density](name:toroidal_co_passing_torque_density).

Sign convention: Positive when the net toroidal force on the counter-passing
population points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: ion_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Particle diffusivity for an ion species, relating its charge-state-summed
diffusive flux to the opposing number-density gradient without selecting a
spatial direction.
items.documentation:
The ion diffusion coefficient characterizes ion particle diffusion through a
local Fickian relation between diffusive particle flux and the
number-density gradient of a specified ion species. It does not select a
spatial direction or a particular transport mechanism.

For a scalar Fickian closure, the defining relation is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_i\nabla n_i
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive ion particle
flux density, $D_i$ is the ion diffusion coefficient, $n_i$ is the ion
number density, and $\nabla$ denotes the spatial gradient. Both flux and
number density are summed over all ionic charge states of the specified
species, excluding neutral particles. The minus sign expresses down-gradient
transport for positive diffusivity.

This is an ion-specific [particle diffusivity](name:particle_diffusivity),
not an ion energy or momentum transport coefficient. It excludes convective
contributions to the ion particle flux. The population is aggregated over
ionic charge states, not over all ion species; the effective coefficient is
not a sum of charge-state diffusion coefficients. In contrast, the [ion
charge-state diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) relates the flux
of one specified charge state to that state's number-density gradient.

The [radial ion diffusion
coefficient](name:radial_ion_diffusion_coefficient) and [poloidal ion
diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_diffusion_coefficient) are
directional diagonal specializations within an anisotropic
particle-diffusion tensor. The scalar closure above applies when a single
coefficient represents the flux-gradient response; the general quantity does
not require equal diffusion in all directions, represent a sum of
directional coefficients, or encode off-diagonal tensor couplings.

items.name: parallel_electron_diffusivity
items.description:
Effective coefficient relating diffusive electron particle flux along the
magnetic field to the electron number-density gradient in that direction.
items.documentation:
Effective parallel electron diffusivity is the directional transport
coefficient describing electron-particle spreading driven by an electron
number-density gradient along the magnetic field. It is the field-parallel
specialization of [electron particle
diffusivity](name:electron_particle_diffusivity) and enters the diffusive
term of the electron density transport equation.

For the field-parallel direction, the diffusive electron particle flux is
defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel,\mathrm{e}}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\parallel,\mathrm{e}}\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{e}}}{\partial s_{\parallel}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\parallel,\mathrm{e}}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the parallel
diffusive electron particle flux, $D_{\parallel,\mathrm{e}}$ is the parallel
electron diffusivity, $n_{\mathrm{e}}$ is electron number density, and
$s_{\parallel}$ is physical arclength increasing along the magnetic-field
direction. For a positive diffusivity, the minus sign specifies transport
down the electron number-density gradient.

This quantity describes density-gradient-driven electron particle transport,
excluding convective particle flux. It is distinct from [parallel electron
energy diffusivity](name:parallel_electron_energy_diffusivity), which
describes diffusive electron thermal-energy transport. Its directional
counterpart, [poloidal electron
diffusivity](name:poloidal_electron_diffusivity), resolves particle
transport in the poloidal direction rather than along the magnetic field.

items.name: normalized_toroidal_beta
items.description:
Normalized toroidal beta scales the whole-plasma toroidal pressure ratio by
minor radius and reference toroidal field relative to plasma current using
the Troyon convention.
items.documentation:
Normalized toroidal beta compares whole-plasma pressure with toroidal
magnetic pressure and applies the Troyon size-and-current normalization. It
is a normalized member of the [beta family](name:beta), rather than an
unmodified pressure ratio.

With dimensional inputs represented by their numerical values in coherent
SI, the defining normalization is

$$\beta = \frac{2\mu_0 \langle p\rangle}{B^2}$$

where $\beta_{\mathrm{N}}$ is normalized toroidal beta, $\beta_{\mathrm{t}}$
is [toroidal beta](name:toroidal_beta), $a$ is the plasma minor radius,
$B_0$ is the reference toroidal magnetic-field magnitude, and $I_p$ is the
total plasma-current magnitude. The factor 100 implements the percentage
convention for beta, while the denominator factor $10^{-6}$ implements the
conventional Troyon current scaling.

The underlying pressure ratio is $\beta_{\mathrm{t}} = 2\mu_0\langle
p\rangle/B_0^2$, where $\mu_0$ is vacuum permeability and $\langle p\rangle$
is total perpendicular plasma pressure averaged over the plasma volume. The
reference field is the same field used in the Troyon normalization.

The pressure includes contributions from all plasma populations, including
thermal and nonthermal populations; thermal-pressure-only normalized beta is
a distinct quantity. This is a global volume-averaged pressure measure, not
a point-local or pedestal beta. It is defined only for nonzero reference
toroidal field and plasma-current magnitude.

items.name: current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction
items.description:
Mechanism-resolved electric current-density vector attributable to
ion–neutral frictional momentum exchange in a partially ionized plasma.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the vector contribution to electric current density
attributed to momentum exchange between plasma ions and neutral particles.
It excludes current contributions assigned to other mechanisms and does not
represent the total plasma current density.

The mechanism-resolved current density is defined from the corresponding
charged-particle velocity contributions:

$$
\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}} = \sum_s q_s n_s \mathbf{v}_{s,\mathrm{in}}
$$

where $q_s$ is the charge of charged species $s$ in C, $n_s$ is its number
density in m$^{-3}$, and $\mathbf{v}_{s,\mathrm{in}}$ is the velocity
contribution attributed to ion–neutral friction. Neutral particles have zero
charge and do not contribute directly to the sum.

The vector may be projected onto cylindrical, poloidal, field-aligned, or
other specified directions, including the [radial current-density
component](name:radial_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction),
[toroidal current-density
component](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction), and
[parallel current-density
component](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction).
Unlike current density due to collisions, its mechanism attribution is
restricted to ion–neutral friction.

items.name: total_electron_density
items.description:
Number density of electrons in the complete free-electron population,
including both thermal and nonthermal contributions and excluding bound
electrons.
items.documentation:
Number density of electron

Total density is the sum of the thermal and fast populations of the species;
thermal excludes the suprathermal particles that fast names.

The total density is defined by

$$
n_e = \int f_e(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_e$ is the total free-electron number density, $f_e$ is the full
electron number distribution in velocity space at the location and time
considered, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element.

The total refers to a sum over electron populations, not a volume-integrated
particle count or a spatial averaging operation. Electrons bound in atoms,
molecules, or ions are excluded. The definition applies in the core, edge,
and scrape-off layer without imposing a particular evaluation location.

This quantity is [electron density](name:electron_density) with the complete
population sum explicitly specified. For an exhaustive, nonoverlapping
thermal and nonthermal decomposition, $n_e = n_{e,\mathrm{th}} +
n_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$, where $n_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is the [thermal electron
density](name:thermal_electron_density) and $n_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the
[fast electron density](name:fast_electron_density). Neither component alone
represents the total.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux
items.description:
Parallel momentum flux for one ion charge state is the net transfer rate per
unit area of field-aligned momentum across a magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Parallel ion charge-state momentum flux across a magnetic flux surface is
the signed transport rate per unit area of magnetic-field-aligned [linear
momentum](name:momentum) carried by ions of one species in one specified
charge state.

It is the field-aligned projection of the [ion charge-state momentum
flux](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux) across the same oriented surface:

$$
\Gamma_{s,\parallel} = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_s = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathsf{T}_s\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state,
$\Gamma_{s,\parallel}$ is this parallel momentum flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_s$ is the vector of momentum transported across the
surface per unit area and time, $\mathsf{T}_s$ is the material momentum-flux
tensor of that ion charge state, $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector along
the magnetic field, and $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the surface-normal unit vector
toward increasing flux-surface label.

The quantity is resolved for one charge state, not summed over charge states
or species. It includes convective and non-convective momentum transport,
rather than only the diffusive contribution or a transport coefficient.
Isotropic pressure contributes no parallel momentum flux across a magnetic
flux surface because the magnetic field is tangent to that surface.

Unlike [poloidal ion charge-state momentum
flux](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux), it selects the
magnetic-field-aligned component of the transported momentum. The transport
is across the flux surface, not along the magnetic field; it is therefore
distinct from [parallel ion charge-state particle
flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux), which describes
along-field number transport.

Sign convention: Positive when the net transfer carries momentum along the
magnetic field toward increasing flux-surface label, or oppositely directed
momentum toward decreasing label.

items.name: volume_averaged_tritium_density
items.description:
Volume-averaged number density of tritium ions over the confined plasma
volume, obtained from the local charge-state-summed fuel-ion density.
items.documentation:
Volume-averaged tritium ion number density quantifies the mean concentration
of hydrogen-3 fuel ions throughout the confined plasma volume. It is the
spatial average of the local [tritium_density](name:tritium_density), rather
than a chord average such as
[line_averaged_tritium_density](name:line_averaged_tritium_density).

$$
\overline{n}_T = \frac{1}{V_c}\int_{V_c} n_T\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_T$ is the volume-averaged tritium ion number density,
$n_T$ is the local tritium ion number density, $V_c$ is the confined plasma
volume bounded by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is the volume
element. The tritium ion density is summed over all ionic charge states and
excludes neutral tritium. This quantity provides the tritium-density basis
for volume-averaged isotopic ratios and is distinct from the local boundary
value
[tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary).

items.name: fast_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional power transferred to the fast
(non-Maxwellian) ion population of a specified species and charge state.
items.documentation:
Volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional power transferred to the fast
(non-Maxwellian) ion population of a specified species and charge state,
obtained by integrating the local Coulomb-collisional energy-exchange rate
density over the plasma volume:

$$
P_{\rm coll,fast}^{s,z} = \int Q_{\rm coll,fast}^{s,z}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $Q_{\rm coll,fast}^{s,z}$ is the local Coulomb-collisional power
density for fast ions of species $s$ in charge state $z$, and $V$ is the
plasma volume. Fast ions are those whose velocity distribution departs
significantly from a Maxwellian, such as neutral-beam-injected or
fusion-born ions undergoing thermalization.

This quantity is the fast-population component of
[total_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions](name:total_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions);
summing it with
[thermal_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions)
recovers the total collisional power for that charge state. Aggregating over
all charge states yields
[fast_ion_power_due_to_collisions](name:fast_ion_power_due_to_collisions).

Sign convention: Positive when net energy is transferred into the fast ion
charge state by Coulomb collisions.

items.name: carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of carbon impurity ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated
locally on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all
ionization states.
items.documentation:
Number density of carbon ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle
count per physical volume for the carbon-ion population evaluated on the
last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the separatrix
separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer.

The defining zeroth velocity-space moment, with explicit aggregation over
carbon ionization states, is

$$
n_C(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{q=1}^{6}\int f_{C^{q+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_C$ is the carbon-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on
the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $q$ is the integer carbon charge-state
index, $f_{C^{q+}}$ is the velocity distribution function of carbon ions in
charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is
the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies locally to carbon ions in charge states C+ through C6+
and is summed over those ionization states. Neutral carbon is excluded, and
the value is not averaged over the boundary flux surface.

It specializes the population-unspecified
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary) to carbon
ions. It is distinct from
flux_surface_averaged_carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary, which applies the
same carbon-ion aggregation after averaging over the boundary surface, and
from [carbon_density](name:carbon_density), whose elemental scope includes
neutral carbon as well as ionic charge states.

items.name: poloidal_current_function
items.description:
Major-radius-weighted toroidal magnetic-field function used in axisymmetric
equilibria and vacuum fields; in ideal-MHD plasma it is constant on each
magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
The poloidal current function is the major-radius-weighted toroidal magnetic
field that defines the equilibrium $F$-function. It provides a common
description for the toroidal field in axisymmetric plasma equilibria and in
current-free vacuum magnetic fields.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the defining relation is

$$
F(R,Z) = R B_\phi(R,Z)
$$

where $F$ is the poloidal current function, $R$ is major radius measured
from the machine symmetry axis, $B_\phi$ is the toroidal component of the
magnetic field, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For an axisymmetric ideal-MHD plasma equilibrium, $F$ is a flux function: it
is constant on each nested magnetic flux surface and can therefore be
expressed as a function of the poloidal magnetic-flux coordinate. The
quantity describes the full toroidal magnetic field represented by the
equilibrium; it is not a surface or volume integral, an average, or a
restriction to a particular current source.

The [vacuum poloidal current
function](name:vacuum_poloidal_current_function) is the corresponding
external-coil contribution in a current-free vacuum region, whereas the
unqualified quantity denotes the general $F$-function. The [product of the
poloidal current function and its derivative with respect to the poloidal
magnetic flux
coordinate](name:product_of_poloidal_current_function_and_derivative_of_poloidal_current_function_with_respect_to_poloidal_magnetic_flux_coordinate)
is a distinct Grad–Shafranov source term formed from $F$ and its flux
derivative.

Sign convention: Positive when $B_\phi$ points in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: toroidal_beryllium_velocity_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Toroidal bulk-flow velocity of beryllium ions at the core-side shoulder of
the H-mode edge transport barrier, density-weighted over all ionization
states.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the beryllium impurity-ion
bulk-flow velocity at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport
barrier, conventionally called the pedestal top.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
V_{\mathrm{Be},\phi} = \frac{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Be},z} v_{\mathrm{Be},z,\phi}}{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Be},z}}
$$

where $z$ indexes the included beryllium ion charge states,
$n_{\mathrm{Be},z}$ is the corresponding number density in m$^{-3}$, and
$v_{\mathrm{Be},z,\phi}$ is the charge-state-resolved toroidal velocity in m
s$^{-1}$. The result is a density-weighted intensive mean, not a sum of
charge-state velocities; the corresponding elemental concentration is
represented by beryllium density at the pedestal top. It is evaluated at the
pedestal top rather than at the magnetic axis, as in [toroidal beryllium
velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_beryllium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).

Sign convention: Positive when the beryllium bulk flow has a component in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: counter_passing_fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Local Coulomb-collisional power density changing the kinetic-energy density
of fast particles on counter-passing guiding-center orbits.
items.documentation:
Counter-passing fast-particle collisional power density is the local rate at
which Coulomb collisions change the kinetic-energy density of fast particles
on counter-passing guiding-center orbits. Counter-passing orbits are passing
trajectories whose parallel transit is opposite to the reference co-passing
direction; this quantity is the collisional source or sink for that orbit
class, not its stored kinetic-energy density.

For fast species $a$, the counter-passing contribution is the kinetic-energy
moment of the Coulomb collision operator restricted to counter-passing phase
space:

$$
P_{\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{a\in\mathrm{fast}} \sum_b \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{counter}}} \frac{1}{2} m_a v^2 C_{ab}[f_a,f_b](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the counter-passing
fast-particle collisional power density at position $\mathbf{x}$, $m_a$ is
the mass of fast species $a$, $v=|\mathbf{v}|$ is speed, $C_{ab}$ is the
Coulomb collision operator giving the collisional time derivative of the
fast-species distribution $f_a$ due to charged partner species $b$, and
$\Omega_{\mathrm{counter}}$ is the counter-passing region of velocity or
guiding-center phase space.

Together with [co-passing fast-particle collisional power
density](name:co_passing_fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions) and
trapped fast-particle collisional power density, it forms the orbit-class
decomposition of [fast-particle collisional power
density](name:fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions):
$P_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = P_{\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{coll}} +
P_{\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}} +
P_{\mathrm{trapped}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$. The partner sum includes only the
charged collision partners represented in the collisional model; a
partner-resolved quantity would use the corresponding single partner
contribution.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions increase the
kinetic-energy density of the counter-passing fast-particle population.

items.name: radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential_imaginary_part
items.description:
Imaginary part of the radial component of the first-order perturbed
magnetic-vector-potential eigenfunction describing a confined-plasma MHD
mode.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the imaginary quadrature of the radial component of a
first-order perturbed magnetic vector potential eigenfunction in the
confined plasma.

The complex radial component is decomposed as

$$
\widetilde{A}_r = A_{r,\mathrm{R}} + i A_{r,\mathrm{I}}
$$

where $\widetilde{A}_r$ is the complex radial component of the perturbed
magnetic vector potential, $A_{r,\mathrm{R}}$ is its real part,
$A_{r,\mathrm{I}}$ is its imaginary part, and $i$ is the imaginary unit.
This quantity is $A_{r,\mathrm{I}}$.

The definition is restricted to the radial component in the confined plasma
and to the selected linear MHD eigenfunction; it is not a sum over vector
components or modes. It excludes the real quadrature and the poloidal and
toroidal components. Together with the real part, it fully specifies the
complex component and is the imaginary-part specialization of the [radial
perturbed plasma magnetic vector
potential](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential).

items.name: electron_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_pumping
items.description:
Rate at which particles represented as equivalent electrons are removed from
the plasma region by wall pumping, giving global electron-equivalent exhaust
throughput.
items.documentation:
The rate at which particles of the electron-equivalent population are
removed from the plasma region by wall pumping is the global scalar
representation of the wall particle-removal flux. It describes pumped
particle exhaust using equivalent-electron counting rather than a local wall
flux density.

The global removal rate is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{e,\mathrm{pump}} = \frac{dN_{e,\mathrm{removed}}}{dt}
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,\mathrm{pump}}$ is the pumped particle-removal rate
expressed in equivalent electrons, $N_{e,\mathrm{removed}}$ is the
cumulative number of electron equivalents removed by wall pumping, and $t$
is time.

This quantity is aggregated over the wall and represents the total pumping
throughput for the electron-equivalent population. The electron-equivalent
basis does not assert that all removed particles are physical electrons, and
the quantity is not an areal flux density, an electrical current, or a rate
for one specified neutral species.

It is the electron-specific specialization of the general [particle-removal
flux at the wall due to pumping](name:particle_rate_at_wall_due_to_pumping).
In contrast, [neutral particle flux at the wall due to
pumping](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_pumping) uses a specified
neutral species as its counting population rather than equivalent-electron
counting.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of nitrogen ions averaged over the last closed magnetic flux
surface bounding the confined plasma, summed over all ion charge states and
excluding neutral nitrogen.
items.documentation:
Number density of nitrogen

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{N}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{N}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, /\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{N}}\rangle$ is the averaged nitrogen-ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{N}}$ is the local nitrogen-ion number density, $S$ is
the plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is
poloidal magnetic flux. The quantity $|\nabla\psi|$ is the magnitude of the
poloidal magnetic-flux gradient, and the closed-integral symbols denote
integration over the complete surface.

This quantity is summed over all nitrogen ion charge states and excludes
neutral nitrogen. It is a flux-surface average rather than the local value
given by [nitrogen ion density at the plasma
boundary](name:nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary), and it is not a volume
or line average. It follows the same species-specific family pattern as
[flux-surface-averaged neon density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary), with
nitrogen replacing neon.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

items.name: electron_critical_temperature_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Temperature of electrons at the pedestal top at which the pedestal reaches
marginal stability against coupled peeling–ballooning modes.
items.documentation:
Temperature of electron at pedestal top

At the transition to instability, the threshold satisfies

$$
\gamma_{\mathrm{PB}}\!\left(T_{e,\mathrm{ped}}^{\mathrm{crit}}\right)=0
$$

where $T_{e,\mathrm{ped}}^{\mathrm{crit}}$ is the critical pedestal-top
electron temperature and $\gamma_{\mathrm{PB}}$ is the growth rate of the
peeling–ballooning mode becoming unstable, with the associated equilibrium
quantities evaluated self-consistently.

The threshold applies to the local electron population at the pedestal top,
not to an average over the pedestal region or over plasma species. Its value
depends on the pedestal pressure and current distributions, including the
self-consistent bootstrap-current contribution; it is not a universal
electron-temperature limit.

The [electron temperature at the pedestal
top](name:electron_temperature_at_pedestal_top) denotes the corresponding
local state quantity and equals this critical value only when the pedestal
lies on the stated stability boundary.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude
items.description:
Geometric metric coefficient formed by averaging the local magnitude of the
toroidal-flux-coordinate gradient over each nested magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the flux-surface average of the local geometric rate at
which the toroidal flux coordinate changes through physical space. It is a
scalar metric coefficient associated with nested magnetic surfaces.

The defining relation is

$$
\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{S}) = \left\langle \left|\nabla \rho_{\mathrm{tor}}\right| \right\rangle_{\mathcal{S}}
$$

where $\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{S})$ is the averaged metric coefficient,
$\mathcal{S}$ is a magnetic flux surface, $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the
toroidal flux coordinate labeling nested magnetic surfaces, $\nabla$ is the
spatial gradient, and the angle brackets with subscript $\mathcal{S}$ denote
averaging over that surface.

The quantity applies to the complete nested magnetic flux surface and is
aggregated over the surface rather than evaluated at a point, along a line,
or over a volume. It represents the average of the gradient magnitude, not a
directional component and not the local unaveraged value.

It is obtained by applying flux-surface averaging to the local [toroidal
flux coordinate gradient
magnitude](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude). Unlike
[flux-surface-averaged square of toroidal flux coordinate gradient
magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude),
it averages the magnitude itself rather than its square.

items.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density
items.description:
Dimensionless hydrogen-isotope fraction equal to the volume-averaged
protium-ion density divided by the volume-averaged density of all hydrogenic
ions.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the fraction of the hydrogenic ion population attributable
to protium, evaluated from volume-averaged densities over the same plasma
volume. The numerator is the [volume-averaged hydrogen
density](name:volume_averaged_hydrogen_density), while the denominator
includes the corresponding hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium ion populations.

$$
f_H = \frac{\overline{n}_H}{\overline{n}_H + \overline{n}_D + \overline{n}_T}
$$

Here $f_H$ is the hydrogen-isotope fraction; $\overline{n}_H$,
$\overline{n}_D$, and $\overline{n}_T$ are the volume-averaged densities of
protium, deuterium, and tritium ions, respectively. The quantity is a ratio
of separately volume-averaged densities, not a local isotope fraction or a
fraction restricted to a single charge state.

items.name: power_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Volume-integrated net power transferred to a plasma particle population
through Coulomb collisions, abstracting over all source and receiving
population combinations without prescribing which species serve as donor or
receiver.
items.documentation:
Coulomb collisions mediate energy exchange between plasma populations —
electrons, thermal ions, fast particles, impurity ions, and neutrals —
converting differential kinetic energy into thermal energy of the receiving
species. This abstract parent captures the general concept of
volume-integrated collisional power transfer without specifying which
populations participate; every concrete child quantity carries explicit
population labels to identify the donor and receiver.

The volume-integrated collisional power is defined as:

$$
P_{\rm coll} = \int_V Q_{\rm coll}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $Q_{\rm coll}$ is the local collisional power exchange density and the
integral extends over the plasma volume $V$.

Concrete population-resolved instances of this quantity include
[ion_power_due_to_collisions](name:ion_power_due_to_collisions), which
covers the total ion population summed over all species and charge states,
and ion_state_power_due_to_collisions, which resolves this to a specified
ionization state. Source-resolved variants such as
[fast_particle_power_due_to_collisions](name:fast_particle_power_due_to_collisions),
[thermal_electron_power_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_electron_power_due_to_collisions),
and
[thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions)
additionally identify the donating population.

Sign convention: Positive when net energy is deposited into the specified
receiving population (net collisional heating); negative when the receiving
population loses energy to others (net collisional cooling).

items.name: toroidal_total_current_density
items.description:
Toroidal total current density is the net conventional charge flux per unit
area around the symmetry axis, formed by algebraically summing all included
current contributions.
items.documentation:
Toroidal total current density is the signed local projection of the net
[current density](name:current_density) onto the toroidal direction. It
combines all included contributions before or after projection onto that
same direction.

The projection and aggregation are defined by:

$$
j_\phi = \hat{\phi}\cdot\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_k \hat{\phi}\cdot\mathbf{j}_k
$$

where $j_\phi$ is the toroidal total current density,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total current-density vector,
$\mathbf{j}_k$ is an included current-density contribution, and $k$ labels
those contributions. The unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ points toward increasing
toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where
$R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The total is an algebraic sum, not a sum of magnitudes, and does not select
a particular species, charge state, or current-generation mechanism. The
quantity is local, with no restriction to a particular plasma region; it is
neither a current-density magnitude nor a flux-surface average or spatially
integrated current.

This quantity specializes [total current
density](name:total_current_density) by fixing its common signed projection
to the toroidal direction. The adjacent [radial total current
density](name:radial_total_current_density) instead projects the same net
charge-flux density onto the outward major-radius direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the net conventional charge transport is in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle, counterclockwise when viewed
from above along the negative vertical direction.

items.name: thermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure
items.description:
Pressure of thermal neutral particles in one specified internal quantum or
excitation state, arising from random translational motion rather than bulk
flow or suprathermal particles.
items.documentation:
Pressure of thermal neutral particles of one species in a specified internal
quantum or excitation state is the isotropic mechanical stress from their
random translational motion. It is the thermal-population component of
[neutral internal-state pressure](name:neutral_internal_state_pressure).

The pressure is defined by the central second velocity moment of the thermal
distribution:

$$
p_{0,a}^{\mathrm{th}} = \frac{m_0}{3}\int |\mathbf{c}|^2 f_{0,a}^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{c})\,d^3c
$$

where $p_{0,a}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the state-resolved thermal neutral
pressure, $m_0$ is the particle mass of the selected neutral species, $a$
labels its internal state, $\mathbf{c}$ is particle velocity relative to the
thermal population's mean flow, $f_{0,a}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is its
number-density distribution in that relative velocity, and $d^3c$ is the
velocity-space volume element. The subscript $0$ denotes neutral particles,
and the superscript $\mathrm{th}$ denotes the thermal population.

The quantity applies to the Maxwellian thermal population in one internal
state, with no sum over internal states or species. In the edge and
scrape-off-layer setting, it is evaluated locally at the outboard equatorial
midplane rather than averaged over a flux surface. It is the state-resolved
counterpart of [thermal neutral pressure](name:thermal_neutral_pressure).

Bulk-flow momentum flux and internal excitation energy are excluded: the
internal state selects the particles but does not contribute excitation
energy to their translational pressure. Unlike [total neutral internal-state
pressure](name:total_neutral_internal_state_pressure), this quantity
excludes the nonthermal contribution described by [suprathermal neutral
internal-state pressure](name:suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure).

items.name: poloidal_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction
items.description:
Poloidal current density due to ion–neutral friction is the signed
electric-charge flux contribution along the local poloidal tangent arising
from momentum exchange between ions and neutrals.
items.documentation:
Poloidal current density due to ion–neutral friction is the poloidal
projection of the [current density due to ion–neutral
friction](name:current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction). It represents
the electric-current contribution attributable to frictional momentum
exchange between plasma ions and neutral particles.

The component is defined by

$$
j_{\mathrm{p}} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{p}}$ is this poloidal current-density contribution,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the ion–neutral-friction current-density
vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the local unit poloidal
tangent directed toward increasing poloidal angle. The tangent lies in a
plane of constant toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The positive poloidal-angle
orientation must be specified independently; the cylindrical basis alone
does not fix it.

This is a local contribution in a partially ionized plasma, without spatial
averaging or integration. It excludes contributions assigned to other
mechanisms and does not represent the total plasma [current
density](name:current_density). The [toroidal current density due to
ion–neutral
friction](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction) is a
different projection of the same mechanism-resolved vector, rather than an
additional mechanism. The poloidal projection is not the
magnetic-field-parallel projection.

Sign convention: Positive when the ion–neutral-friction contribution carries
conventional electric current along the local poloidal tangent toward
increasing poloidal angle.

items.name: poloidal_ion_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Dimensionless coefficient scaling the free-streaming upper bound on the flux
of poloidal momentum carried by a specified ion state in edge plasma.
items.documentation:
This coefficient sets the free-streaming bound used to limit the flux of
poloidal [momentum](name:momentum) carried by one specified ion state in
edge plasma. It is the state-resolved poloidal member of the [momentum flux
limiter coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) family.

The limited momentum flux satisfies:

$$
\left|\Pi_{s,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{lim}}\right| \leq \alpha_{s,\mathrm{p}}\Pi_{s,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion state, $\mathrm{p}$ denotes the poloidal
momentum component, $\Pi_{s,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is its limited flux
across an oriented surface, $\alpha_{s,\mathrm{p}}$ is this nonnegative
limiter coefficient, and $\Pi_{s,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the
nonnegative free-streaming reference flux magnitude. Limiting reduces the
flux magnitude without reversing its direction; the coefficient does not
specify a unique interpolation between unrestricted and limited fluxes.

Poloidal identifies the transported momentum component, not the direction in
which momentum crosses the oriented surface. The coefficient is neither the
momentum flux itself nor a momentum diffusivity.

The selected ion state may distinguish ionization or other internal states.
This coefficient applies to that state alone, without aggregation over
states, unlike the species-level [poloidal ion momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient). When the
state is specifically a charge state, the corresponding specialization is
the [poloidal ion charge-state momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

items.name: neutral_momentum_flux
items.description:
Rate per unit area at which neutral atoms and molecules transport linear
momentum across an oriented surface in the edge plasma, combining convective
and isotropic-pressure contributions summed over all neutral species and
internal states.
items.documentation:
The neutral momentum flux describes the rate at which the collective neutral
population transports linear momentum across a unit area of an oriented
surface in the edge plasma. It captures both the directed convective flow of
neutral particles and the isotropic thermal pressure of the neutral gas,
aggregated over all neutral species and their internal quantum states.

The neutral momentum-flux tensor $\overleftrightarrow{\Pi}_n$ is:

$$
\overleftrightarrow{\Pi}_n = m_n n_n \mathbf{v}_n \mathbf{v}_n + p_n \mathbf{I}
$$

where $m_n$ is the neutral particle mass, $n_n$ is the neutral number
density, $\mathbf{v}_n$ is the bulk neutral velocity, $p_n = n_n k_B T_n$ is
the neutral thermal pressure with $T_n$ the neutral temperature, and
$\mathbf{I}$ is the identity tensor. The divergence of this tensor drives
the neutral momentum balance equation and couples neutral dynamics to the
ion fluid through charge-exchange and elastic collisions.

This quantity is evaluated within edge fluid or kinetic neutral transport
models rather than measured directly. Directional projections include
toroidal_neutral_momentum_flux,
[poloidal_neutral_momentum_flux](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_flux),
[vertical_neutral_momentum_flux](name:vertical_neutral_momentum_flux), and
[parallel_neutral_momentum_flux](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_flux) along
the local magnetic-field direction. The analogous ion-fluid momentum
transport rate is
[radial_edge_ion_momentum_flux](name:radial_ion_momentum_flux_over_edge_region),
while the effective convective transport coefficient for neutral momentum is
radial_neutral_effective_momentum_convection_velocity.

items.name: vertical_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Dimensionless flux-limiter coefficient that scales the free-streaming bound
on the vertical (Z) momentum-flux-density component in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame for a specified neutral particle state in
edge-plasma transport closures.
items.documentation:
The vertical neutral-state momentum coefficient is a dimensionless
flux-limiter factor assigned to a specified neutral particle state in
edge-plasma transport closures. It scales the free-streaming bound on the
magnitude of the vertical component of momentum-flux density, where the
component is projected along $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame, preventing unphysical supersonic neutral-momentum transport
without changing the direction carried by the modeled flux.

The defining relation for the vertical projection is:

$$
\Pi_Z = c_Z \, \Pi_Z^{\rm FS}
$$

where $\Pi_Z$ is the modeled vertical momentum-flux-density component of the
specified neutral particle state, $\Pi_Z^{\rm FS}$ is the corresponding
free-streaming momentum-flux-density component, and $c_Z$ is the vertical
neutral-state momentum coefficient.

It is the vertical projection component of the vector [neutral-state
momentum
coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient_over_edge_region).
It is distinct from the [radial neutral-state momentum
coefficient](name:radial_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
[toroidal neutral-state momentum
coefficient](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
[poloidal neutral-state momentum
coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
and [parallel neutral-state momentum
coefficient](name:parallel_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
which apply the same limiter concept to other projection directions.

When flux limiting is active, $c_Z$ is bounded in $[0, 1]$: $c_Z = 1$ leaves
the free-streaming bound unscaled, while smaller values impose a stronger
limiter on the vertical momentum-flux-density magnitude. The coefficient is
non-negative; the sign of the vertical momentum-flux-density component is
carried by $\Pi_Z$ rather than by $c_Z$.

items.name: perturbed_plasma_pressure_imaginary_part
items.description:
Imaginary part of the complex first-order plasma pressure perturbation
eigenfunction for a specified toroidal Fourier mode in linear MHD stability
analysis.
items.documentation:
The perturbed plasma pressure $\tilde{p}$ is the complex scalar
eigenfunction representing the linearized first-order pressure perturbation
for a single toroidal mode number $n$ in a linear MHD stability calculation.
The total pressure decomposes as $p = p_0 +
\mathrm{Re}[\tilde{p}\,e^{i(n\phi - \omega t)}]$, where $p_0$ is the
equilibrium pressure profile, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $\omega$ is the complex
eigenfrequency.

This quantity is the imaginary component of $\tilde{p}$ under the standard
complex decomposition:

$$
\tilde{p} = \mathrm{Re}(\tilde{p}) + i\,\mathrm{Im}(\tilde{p})
$$

where both $\mathrm{Re}(\tilde{p})$ and $\mathrm{Im}(\tilde{p})$ are
real-valued scalar fields resolved on the two-dimensional poloidal
cross-section. Combined with
[perturbed_plasma_pressure_real_part](name:perturbed_plasma_pressure_real_part),
this quantity fully specifies the complex pressure perturbation amplitude at
each grid point for the given mode.

The imaginary part encodes the local spatial phase of the pressure
perturbation relative to the phase reference convention of the linear MHD
eigenvalue solver. Eigenfunction normalization is solver-dependent, so
absolute amplitudes are physically meaningful only when a normalization
convention is explicitly fixed. This quantity is structurally analogous to
[perturbed_plasma_mass_density_imaginary_part](name:perturbed_plasma_mass_density_imaginary_part)
and
[perturbed_plasma_temperature_imaginary_part](name:perturbed_plasma_temperature_imaginary_part),
which follow the same Fourier decomposition for their respective physical
scalars.

Sign convention: Positive when $\mathrm{Im}(\tilde{p}) > 0$ under the
decomposition $\tilde{p} = \mathrm{Re}(\tilde{p}) +
i\,\mathrm{Im}(\tilde{p})$ with toroidal Fourier factor $e^{in\phi}$, where
$\phi$ increases counter-clockwise viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$.

items.name: total_thermal_ion_density
items.description:
Number density of thermal ions summed over all ion species and positive
charge states, excluding fast ions and neutral particles.
items.documentation:
Number density of ion

The species-and-charge-state sum is defined by

$$
n_{i,\mathrm{th},\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_s \sum_{q\geq 1} n_{s,q,\mathrm{th}}
$$

where $n_{i,\mathrm{th},\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total thermal ion number
density, $i$ identifies the ion population, $s$ labels an ion species, $q$
is its positive integer charge state, and $n_{s,q,\mathrm{th}}$ is the
thermal number density of that species in that charge state.

The definition applies in confined plasma and the scrape-off layer. The
total denotes aggregation over species and charge states, not spatial
integration; no spatial averaging is implied. Neutral particles and
nonthermal ions are excluded, including the population described by [fast
ion density](name:fast_ion_density).

This quantity is the sum of the species-specific [thermal ion
densities](name:thermal_ion_density), rather than the density of one
selected species. It differs from [line-averaged total ion
density](name:line_averaged_total_ion_density), which averages along a
specified chord and includes both thermal and nonthermal ions.

items.name: poloidal_ion_particle_flux
items.description:
Poloidal ion particle flux is the signed net ion crossing rate per area
normal to the local poloidal direction for one species, summed over all
ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Poloidal ion particle flux is the local net number flow of one specified ion
species through a surface perpendicular to the local poloidal direction,
divided by that surface's area. It includes thermal and nonthermal ions and
counts oppositely directed crossings with opposite signs.

The poloidal projection and charge-state aggregation are defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{i,\mathrm p} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i \cdot \hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p} = \sum_{z>0}\Gamma_{i,z,\mathrm p}
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,\mathrm p}$ is the species-level poloidal ion particle
flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i$ is the ion number-flux vector for species $i$,
$\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}$ is the local positive poloidal unit vector,
$z$ is the ionic charge number, and $\Gamma_{i,z,\mathrm p}$ is the
[poloidal ion charge-state particle
flux](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) for that species and
charge state.

The sum includes all ionic charge states of the selected species, excludes
neutral particles, and does not aggregate different species. This quantity
is [ion particle flux](name:ion_particle_flux) evaluated with the surface
normal aligned with the local poloidal direction; it is not an
electric-charge flux, a surface-integrated particle rate, or a flux-surface
average.

The poloidal direction lies in a plane of constant toroidal angle in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical position. Its positive
orientation follows increasing poloidal angle $\theta$; the orientation
chosen for $\theta$ must be specified. A poloidal projection is not, in
general, a magnetic-field-parallel or flux-surface-normal projection.

Sign convention: Positive when the net ion number flow is directed along
increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

items.name: sawtooth_period
items.description:
Time interval between successive sawtooth crash events, representing the
duration of one complete sawtooth oscillation cycle in a tokamak plasma.
items.documentation:
The sawtooth period is the elapsed time from one sawtooth crash to the next
consecutive crash, including the intervening growth and relaxation phases.

For successive crash times $t_k$ and $t_{k+1}$, the period is defined by

$$
T_{\mathrm{st}} = t_{k+1} - t_k
$$

where $T_{\mathrm{st}}$ is the sawtooth period and $t_k$ is the time of the
$k$th crash. The quantity refers to the temporal spacing of consecutive
crash events, not the duration of the crash itself or the duration of the
preceding growth phase alone.

items.name: effective_charge
items.description:
Effective charge of a plasma mixture is its second ionic charge-number
moment normalized by free-electron density, expressing the composition
factor for electron–ion Coulomb scattering.
items.documentation:
Effective charge characterizes the charge-state composition of a plasma ion
mixture through its contribution to electron–ion Coulomb scattering. It
encompasses local values and explicitly specified spatial averages of those
values.

The underlying local effective charge is defined by:

$$
Z_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{\sum_s n_s Z_s^2}{n_e}
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the effective charge, $s$ labels each ion
species and charge-state population, $n_s$ is that population's number
density, $Z_s$ is its ionic charge number relative to the positive
elementary charge, and $n_e$ is the free-electron number density at the same
location.

The summation includes all ion species and charge states present, rather
than a selected species or charge state. Effective charge is neither a
single ion's charge number nor the net electric charge of the plasma.
Locus-specific quantities, such as [effective charge at the plasma
boundary](name:effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary), evaluate this
definition at their stated location.

For a quasineutral mixture of electrons and positive ions, $n_e = \sum_s n_s
Z_s$, making effective charge a charge-density-weighted mean ionic charge
number. It equals one when all ions are singly charged.

[Volume-averaged effective charge](name:volume_averaged_effective_charge)
averages the local effective charge over the confined plasma volume; a
global value inferred from ohmic resistive flux consumption during an ohmic
phase represents this volume-averaged instance. [Line-averaged effective
charge](name:line_averaged_effective_charge) instead averages it uniformly
along a specified line of sight. Neither averaging convention is implicit in
the unqualified quantity.

items.name: kinetic_energy_density
items.description:
Kinetic energy carried by a specified particle population per unit volume,
combining random thermal motion with directed or nonthermal translational
motion.
items.documentation:
Kinetic energy density is the translational kinetic energy carried by a
defined particle population per unit volume. It includes random thermal
motion and directed or nonthermal motion represented within that population.

The local kinetic energy density is defined from the particle velocity
distribution by

$$
K_{\mathrm{kin}}(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \int \varepsilon_{\mathrm{kin},s}(\mathbf{v})\, f_s(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})\, d^3v
$$

where $K_{\mathrm{kin}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the kinetic energy density at
position $\mathbf{r}$, $\mathcal{S}$ is the set of included particle species
or states, $s$ identifies one member of that set,
$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{kin},s}(\mathbf{v})$ is the translational kinetic
energy of a particle with velocity $\mathbf{v}$, and
$f_s(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})$ is its velocity-distribution density.

The population and aggregation are defined by the specific application:
species and charge states may be summed, while a designated population such
as runaway electrons may be represented by its population mean. The quantity
may be evaluated locally or resolved by magnetic flux surface; neither
spatial representation changes its kinetic-energy definition. The [ion
kinetic energy density](name:ion_kinetic_energy_density) is the
ion-population instance, while the [runaway electron kinetic energy
density](name:runaway_electron_kinetic_energy_density) is the
runaway-electron instance.

This component of [energy density](name:energy_density) includes
translational particle motion only. It excludes magnetic, electric,
potential, and non-translational internal-state energy, while random thermal
motion remains included when it belongs to the specified particle
population.

items.name: thermal_radiative_power_of_divertor
