items.description:
Thermal radiation emitted by all divertor target surfaces, with each surface
contribution weighted by its emissivity and summed over the divertor.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the total thermal radiative power emitted by the surfaces
of all divertor targets. It represents surface emission governed by the
local surface temperature and emissivity.

$$
P_{\mathrm{bb}} = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{D}} \int_{A_i} \epsilon_i\,\sigma_{\mathrm{SB}}\,T_i^4\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{bb}}$ is the emitted thermal radiative power,
$\mathcal{D}$ is the set of divertor target surfaces, $A_i$ is the surface
area of target $i$, $\epsilon_i$ is its local thermal emissivity,
$\sigma_{\mathrm{SB}}$ is the Stefan–Boltzmann constant, $T_i$ is its local
absolute surface temperature, and $\mathrm{d}A$ is a surface-area element.

The quantity is aggregated over every divertor target surface and includes
emissivity effects. It describes radiation emitted by the targets, not
plasma power incident on them or radiation retained after reflection.

It is distinct from [absorbed radiated power of the
divertor](name:absorbed_radiated_power_of_divertor), which is the net
radiative power deposited on the targets after accounting for incident and
reflected radiation, and from [total incident power of the
divertor](name:total_incident_power_of_divertor), which describes incoming
plasma power rather than surface emission.

items.name: thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power
items.description:
Total coherent-wave power absorbed by the bulk thermal (Maxwellian) ion
population, integrated over the plasma volume.
items.documentation:
The thermal ion absorbed wave power is the volume-integrated power delivered
by coherent electromagnetic waves to the bulk thermal (approximately
Maxwellian) ion population via wave-particle resonance interactions. It is
the thermal-ion component of
[ion_absorbed_wave_power](name:ion_absorbed_wave_power), which spans all ion
populations.

$$
P_{\mathrm{th,i}} = \int_{V} p_{\mathrm{th,i}}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{th,i}}$ is the local wave power density absorbed by
thermal ions and $V$ is the total plasma volume. The associated spatial
deposition profile is described by
[thermal_ion_power_density](name:thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power_density).

This quantity excludes power deposited into suprathermal (fast) ions. No
ion-species qualifier is carried: it aggregates over all thermal ion species
present in the plasma. Charge-state-resolved contributions are provided by
[thermal_ion_charge_state_power](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power);
summing over all charge states and species recovers this global value.

items.name: toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary_due_to_poloidal_current
items.description:
Signed toroidal magnetic flux through the poloidal cross-section enclosed by
the plasma boundary, attributable specifically to plasma poloidal current.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the contribution to the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by
the plasma boundary that is generated by the plasma poloidal current. It is
a component of the [toroidal magnetic flux at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary), distinct from
contributions attributed to other physical processes.

The contribution is defined by

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{pol}} = \int_{A_b} B_{\phi}^{\mathrm{pol}}\,\mathrm{d}A_p
$$

where $A_b$ is the poloidal cross-sectional area enclosed by the plasma
boundary, $B_{\phi}^{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the toroidal magnetic-field component
generated by the poloidal plasma current, and $\mathrm{d}A_p$ is the
oriented area element of that cross-section. The toroidal direction is
$\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity excludes toroidal-flux contributions attributed to other
mechanisms, such as the [toroidal magnetic flux due to diamagnetic
drift](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), and is not
necessarily the total boundary flux.

Sign convention: Positive when $B_{\phi}^{\mathrm{pol}}$ points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ through the poloidal
cross-section oriented with normal $+\hat{\phi}$.

items.name: vacuum_magnetic_field
items.description:
Local magnetic-induction vector generated by currents external to the plasma
with plasma-current contributions omitted, retaining field strength and
direction before selecting a component in the right-handed cylindrical (R,
φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The vacuum magnetic field $\mathbf{B}_{\rm vac}$ is the local [magnetic
induction](name:magnetic_field) generated by currents external to the plasma
when plasma-current contributions are omitted. It represents a vector field
at a point, retaining field strength and direction rather than selecting a
cylindrical component or scalar magnitude.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the vacuum field may be
resolved as

$$
\mathbf{B}_{\rm vac}=B_{R,{\rm vac}}\hat{R}+B_{\phi,{\rm vac}}\hat{\phi}+B_{Z,{\rm vac}}\hat{Z}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}_{\rm vac}$ is the vacuum magnetic field, $B_{R,{\rm vac}}$
is its signed radial component, $B_{\phi,{\rm vac}}$ is the [toroidal vacuum
magnetic field](name:toroidal_vacuum_magnetic_field), $B_{Z,{\rm vac}}$ is
its signed vertical component, and $\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, and $\hat{Z}$
are the basis vectors for increasing major radius, toroidal angle, and
vertical height.

This quantity is the externally sourced, plasma-current-omitted contribution
to the local field and may be evaluated inside the confined-plasma region as
well as in vacuum regions; it does not denote only the space outside the
plasma. It has no species population, and its aggregation convention is a
local point value, not a spatial average, flux-surface average, or
finite-volume reduction.

It is distinct from the [plasma magnetic field](name:plasma_magnetic_field),
which represents the magnetic-field contribution associated with the
confined plasma, and from the unrestricted local [magnetic
induction](name:magnetic_field), which does not by name isolate the vacuum
contribution. The [non-axisymmetric magnetic
field](name:non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field) is the toroidally varying part
of the external-coil vacuum field after its toroidally averaged component is
removed, while a [perturbed vacuum magnetic
field](name:perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field) denotes a perturbative vacuum
contribution rather than the full vacuum vector.

The [vacuum magnetic vector
potential](name:vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential) $\mathbf{A}_{\rm vac}$ is
a potential for this field, with $\mathbf{B}_{\rm
vac}=\nabla\times\mathbf{A}_{\rm vac}$, where $\mathbf{A}_{\rm vac}$ is the
vacuum magnetic vector potential and $\nabla$ is the spatial differential
operator. Different gage choices of $\mathbf{A}_{\rm vac}$ that have the
same curl represent the same vacuum magnetic field; in regions containing no
external current density, $\mathbf{B}_{\rm vac}$ is curl-free, and the field
is solenoidal.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component of $\mathbf{B}_{\rm
vac}$ points along the corresponding positive basis vector of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where the positive directions
are increasing major radius $R$, increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, and
increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: radial_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport
items.description:
Radial current density due to anomalous transport is the signed
conventional-charge flux along the major-radius direction attributed to
turbulent, nonclassical plasma transport.
items.documentation:
Radial current density due to anomalous transport is the signed major-radius
projection of the conventional electric-current contribution attributed to
turbulent, nonclassical plasma transport.

The defining projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height, is

$$
j_R = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}} \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $j_R$ is the radial current density due to anomalous transport,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}}$ is the [current-density vector due to anomalous
transport](name:current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport), and $\hat{R}$
is the unit vector toward increasing major radius.

This local plasma quantity represents the net conventional-charge flux
attributed to anomalous transport, not the [current
density](name:current_density) summed over all mechanisms. No spatial
averaging or integration is implied. The major-radius direction is not
generally normal to a magnetic flux surface or perpendicular to the magnetic
field.

Together with the
[toroidal](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport) and
[vertical](name:vertical_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport) current
densities due to anomalous transport, it specifies the cylindrical
components of the same anomalous-current vector.

Sign convention: Positive when conventional electric current attributed to
anomalous transport flows toward increasing major radius, away from the
toroidal symmetry axis.

items.name: wave_current_of_antenna_strap
items.description:
Characterization of the radio-frequency current oscillating along an antenna
strap, encompassing peak-amplitude and root-mean-square representations of
the same wave current.
items.documentation:
Wave current of an antenna strap is the radio-frequency electric current
oscillating along the strap conductor during electromagnetic-wave
excitation. The quantity is represented by a non-negative measure of the
oscillation rather than by the instantaneous signed waveform.

The underlying single-frequency current can be represented as

$$
I_{\mathrm{RF}}(t) = \operatorname{Re}\{\widetilde{I}_{\mathrm{RF}} e^{i\omega t}\}
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{RF}}(t)$ is the instantaneous radio-frequency current,
$\widetilde{I}_{\mathrm{RF}}$ is its complex phasor, $t$ is time, and
$\omega$ is the angular frequency of the oscillation.

This quantity applies to the radio-frequency current carried by an antenna
strap and includes representations evaluated at a strap position or formed
as an effective measure of the oscillation. It excludes the non-wave or
total current represented by [current of an antenna
strap](name:current_of_antenna_strap), as well as current density and plasma
current.

The accepted child quantities provide two representations of this common
quantity: [wave current amplitude of an antenna
strap](name:wave_current_amplitude_of_antenna_strap) gives the peak
magnitude of the oscillation, while [root-mean-square wave current of an
antenna strap](name:root_mean_square_wave_current_of_antenna_strap) gives
its effective magnitude. For a sinusoidal waveform, the root-mean-square
magnitude is the peak magnitude divided by $\sqrt{2}$.

items.name: neutron_maximum_energy_of_neutron_detector
items.description:
High-energy endpoint of the neutron kinetic-energy interval assigned to a
neutron detector energy band.
items.documentation:
The maximum neutron energy of a detector band is the upper kinetic-energy
boundary used to classify energy-resolved neutron counts. It is an
instrumental band limit, not the maximum energy present in the neutron
population.

The selected energy interval is bounded by

$$
E_{\min} \leq E_n \leq E_{\max}
$$

where $E_n$ is neutron kinetic energy, $E_{\min}$ is the lower band
boundary, and $E_{\max}$ is this quantity. The lower boundary is represented
by lower-bound neutron-detector energy; neutron-detector energy denotes a
band boundary without specifying which edge.

items.name: parallel_neutral_momentum_source
items.description:
Signed rate of momentum transfer per transport area along the local magnetic
field to an edge-plasma neutral population, summed over all neutral internal
states.
items.documentation:
The parallel neutral momentum source is the signed, area-normalized rate at
which [momentum](name:momentum) is added to or removed from the represented
neutral population along the local magnetic field in the edge plasma. It is
the field-parallel projection of the state-summed vector source.

The projection and internal-state aggregation are defined by:

$$
S_{0,\parallel}=\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf S_0=\sum_{a\in\mathcal N_0}\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf S_{0,a}
$$

where $S_{0,\parallel}$ is this parallel source, $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the
unit vector along the local magnetic field, $\mathbf S_0$ is the [neutral
momentum source](name:neutral_momentum_source), $\mathcal N_0$ is the set of
all internal states of the represented neutral species, $a$ labels one such
state, and $\mathbf S_{0,a}$ is its area-normalized vector momentum source.

The aggregation is a sum over neutral internal states, not a
density-weighted mean or a single-state contribution. Charged-particle
source terms are excluded. This quantity describes momentum input to the
neutral population, not momentum transported across a surface, and its area
normalization distinguishes it from a volumetric force density.

Unlike the [poloidal neutral momentum
source](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_source), which uses the geometric
poloidal direction, this component uses the local magnetic-field direction.
That direction defines the projection even though the particles are
electrically neutral.

Sign convention: Positive when the net momentum transfer to the neutral
population points along the local magnetic field.

items.name: toroidal_center_of_mass_velocity
items.description:
Signed flow around the symmetry axis, equal to the mass-density-weighted
mean of the toroidal velocities of all constituent plasma species.
items.documentation:
The toroidal center-of-mass velocity is the component of the multicomponent
plasma's [center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity) around the
symmetry axis. It retains the mass-density weighting of the full barycentric
velocity.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance
from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height, the defining projection is

$$
V_{\mathrm{cm},\phi} = \mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}\cdot\hat{\phi} = \frac{\sum_s \rho_s\,\mathbf{V}_s\cdot\hat{\phi}}{\sum_s \rho_s}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{cm},\phi}$ is the toroidal center-of-mass velocity,
$\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is the full center-of-mass velocity vector, $s$
indexes constituent species, $\rho_s$ is each species' mass density,
$\mathbf{V}_s$ is its mean velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector
directed toward increasing toroidal angle.

The sum includes all species in the plasma mixture, not only ions. This is a
local mass-density-weighted mean, not a particle-number-weighted mean or an
unweighted sum of species velocities. The definition requires nonzero total
mass density and a position away from the symmetry axis, where the toroidal
direction is defined.

The [bulk center-of-mass velocity](name:bulk_center_of_mass_velocity) is the
corresponding full vector; this projection excludes its cylindrical radial
and vertical components. It is distinct from the vector's speed and from an
angular rotation rate.

Sign convention: Positive when the center-of-mass flow component points
toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, counter-clockwise when viewed from
above the $+Z$ side.

items.name: coolant_pressure
items.description:
Absolute static pressure of the coolant or working fluid at a plant-system
component port, referenced to perfect vacuum rather than atmospheric or
another gage reference.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the local thermodynamic pressure of the coolant or working
fluid at a component-port interface, with perfect vacuum as the
zero-pressure reference. Static pressure is the isotropic mechanical stress
of the fluid and excludes kinetic-energy contributions associated with bulk
flow.

$$
\boldsymbol{\sigma}=-p_{\mathrm{abs}}\mathbf{I}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ is the isotropic fluid Cauchy stress,
$p_{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the absolute static pressure, and $\mathbf{I}$ is the
identity tensor.

The value represents local pressure at the port, not stagnation pressure,
pressure drop, or pressure difference. At a cooling-circuit inlet, it is
related to cooling-circuit inlet pressure, while coolant flow through a
plant component port describes mass transport rather than mechanical
pressure.

items.name: thickness_of_passive_loop_element
items.description:
Transverse dimension of the rectangular cross-section used to represent each
passive conductor loop element, measured perpendicular to its central
segment.
items.documentation:
The thickness is the transverse extent of an individual passive conductor
loop element's rectangular cross-section, measured in the direction
perpendicular to its central segment.

The thickness $t$ is defined by the separation of the two opposing
cross-section boundaries:

$$
t = \left|\mathbf{x}_{\perp,2} - \mathbf{x}_{\perp,1}\right|
$$

where $\mathbf{x}_{\perp,1}$ and $\mathbf{x}_{\perp,2}$ are the positions of
the opposing boundaries along the direction perpendicular to the central
segment, and $t$ is their separation.

This quantity applies to one passive loop element and describes a
cross-sectional dimension; it is not an aggregate over the loop or over
multiple elements. It excludes the longitudinal extent of the element and is
distinct from the [minor length of the passive loop
element](name:minor_length_of_passive_loop_element), which describes an
in-plane side length rather than the transverse thickness.

items.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_krypton_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
items.description:
Volume-averaged krypton density divided by volume-averaged electron density
is the plasma-volume krypton abundance ratio relative to electrons, with
krypton number density summed over all charge states.
items.documentation:
Volume-averaged krypton density divided by volume-averaged electron density
is the plasma-volume krypton abundance ratio formed from the same averaging
volume for krypton and electrons. The krypton density is the species-level
krypton number density summed over all charge states, including neutral
through fully stripped krypton.

The ratio is defined by the quotient of the two volume averages:

$$
f_{\mathrm{Kr},V} = \frac{\langle n_{\mathrm{Kr}} \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V} = \frac{V_p^{-1}\int_{V_p}\sum_{q=0}^{Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}} n_{\mathrm{Kr},q}(\mathbf{x})\,dV}{V_p^{-1}\int_{V_p} n_e(\mathbf{x})\,dV}
$$

where $f_{\mathrm{Kr},V}$ is this krypton abundance ratio, $\langle
n_{\mathrm{Kr}} \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged krypton
density](name:volume_averaged_krypton_density), $\langle n_e \rangle_V$ is
the [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $V_p$ is the averaging
plasma volume, $n_{\mathrm{Kr},q}$ is the krypton number density in charge
state $q$, $q=0$ denotes neutral krypton, $q=Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ denotes fully
stripped krypton, $Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the nuclear charge of krypton, $n_e$
is the electron number density, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, and $dV$
is an infinitesimal volume element.

This quantity applies to the krypton and electron populations inside the
same plasma volume $V_p$. Its aggregation convention is volumetric averaging
for both numerator and denominator; because krypton density is an extensive
per-volume species amount, the species-level krypton density is
charge-state-summed before the volume average is taken.

It is not normalized by the maximum local electron density and is not a
krypton-to-electron density ratio at a single position. It is also distinct
from [line-averaged krypton density](name:line_averaged_krypton_density),
which averages krypton density along a path rather than over the plasma
volume.

The numerator is exactly [volume-averaged krypton
density](name:volume_averaged_krypton_density), and the denominator is
exactly [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density). Replacing the denominator
by a maximum electron density gives the related but different ratio of
volume-averaged krypton density to maximum electron density.

items.name: parallel_ion_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Field-parallel projection of the effective velocity coefficient for
advective ion momentum transport, distinct from the bulk ion flow velocity.
items.documentation:
The parallel ion momentum convection velocity is the signed field-aligned
component of the effective coefficient governing advective, non-diffusive
transport of ion [momentum](name:momentum). It is a transport-closure
coefficient, not the material bulk ion flow velocity.

It is the projection of the parent vector onto the local magnetic-field
direction:

$$
V_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \mathbf{V}_i^{\mathrm{conv}} \cdot \frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $V_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this parallel coefficient,
$\mathbf{V}_i^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the [ion momentum convection
velocity](name:ion_momentum_convection_velocity), $\mathbf{B}$ is the local
magnetic-field vector, and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude. The subscript
$i$ identifies the specified ion species; the projection requires a nonzero
magnetic field.

The species-level intensive coefficient is the density-weighted mean over
all ionic charge states, not a sum of velocities. In contrast, the [parallel
ion charge-state momentum convection
velocity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity)
applies to one specified charge state. This species-level quantity does not
aggregate electron or neutral momentum transport.

Within the advective closure, this coefficient relates the convective
momentum flux along the magnetic field to the transported ion momentum
density. It is distinct from the [momentum
diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity), which describes gradient-driven
diffusive transport, and is not itself a momentum flux or momentum source.

Sign convention: Positive when the effective ion momentum convection
velocity has a component in the direction of the local magnetic field.

items.name: counter_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force
items.description:
Angular-momentum source per unit volume generated by the Lorentz force,
averaged over a magnetic flux surface for counter-passing particles.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged torque density transferred to
counter-passing particles by the magnetic Lorentz force associated with
their current contribution. Counter-passing particles are the orbit
population whose parallel motion is opposite the plasma-current direction.

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{J\times B}^{\mathrm{cp}}(\psi)=\left\langle\mathbf{r}\times\left(\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{cp}}\times\mathbf{B}\right)\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{J\times B}^{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the torque-density
vector, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the selected torque origin,
$\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the current-density contribution associated
with counter-passing particles, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, and
$\psi$ labels the magnetic flux surface. The angle brackets denote a
flux-surface average.

This orbit-resolved vector is a member of the [torque density due to J×B
force](name:torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) family. Its toroidal
projection is represented by [toroidal counter-passing torque density due to
J×B
force](name:toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force),
while [co-passing torque density due to J×B
force](name:co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) describes the
corresponding population with parallel motion along the plasma-current
direction.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved torque component points in the
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field
items.description:
Toroidal component of the complex first-order magnetic-field perturbation
eigenfunction in the current-free vacuum region outside the plasma, resolved
for a single toroidal Fourier mode number in linear MHD stability analysis.
items.documentation:
The toroidal projection $\delta B_\phi = \delta\mathbf{B} \cdot \hat{\phi}$
of the linearized magnetic-field perturbation in the current-free vacuum
surrounding the plasma constitutes one scalar component of the full
perturbed vacuum magnetic-field vector. In the vacuum exterior, $\nabla
\times \delta\mathbf{B} = 0$, so $\delta\mathbf{B}$ is derivable from a
scalar magnetic potential satisfying Laplace's equation; the toroidal
component is determined by matching conditions at the plasma-vacuum
interface and at any conducting wall boundaries. The eigenfunction is
complex-valued, and this parent quantity abstracts over its two real-valued
projections:
[toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part)
and
[toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part),
which carry the in-phase and quadrature contributions of the mode structure
relative to the toroidal reference angle $\phi$. This projection is one
component of the full
[perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field](name:perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field)
vector, alongside the poloidal and radial components captured by
[poloidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part](name:poloidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part)
and
[radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part).
Computed by solving the vacuum Maxwell equations exterior to the plasma
boundary in linear MHD stability analysis; the absolute amplitude is
normalization-dependent, while the relative phase between vacuum and plasma
regions carries reconnection information relevant to resistive and
resistive-wall modes.

Sign convention: Positive when $\delta B_\phi$ points in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: helium_4_density_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Number density of helium-4 ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance, summed over singly and doubly
ionized states and excluding neutral helium-4.
items.documentation:
Number density of helium-4 ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the helium-4-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The helium-4 ion number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{He4}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{He4}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the helium-4 ion number density,
$N_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the number of helium-4 ions, and $V$ is a small plasma
volume whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side.

This quantity applies to the ionized helium-4 population immediately
adjacent to the divertor target and is summed over the singly and doubly
ionized charge states, with each ion counted once. Neutral helium-4 atoms
are excluded, so this quantity is not the total helium-4 particle density
including neutrals or a charge density.

As a species-specific specialization, this quantity contributes to the
broader [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target) family
without including other ion species. The isotope distinction from
[helium_3_density_at_divertor_target](name:helium_3_density_at_divertor_target)
is maintained; the two quantities describe different helium isotopes.

items.name: lithium_density_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Number density of the lithium species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for ionized lithium at the sheath entrance, summed
over positive ionization states and excluding neutral lithium.
items.documentation:
Number density of the lithium species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for ionized lithium at the sheath entrance
immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the
lithium-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local lithium-ion number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Li}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Li}}}{dV}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the number of ionized lithium ions in the local
plasma volume $V$, with the count summed over all positive lithium
ionization states.

This quantity applies to the ionized lithium population immediately adjacent
to the divertor target and uses a charge-state-summed aggregation. Neutral
lithium atoms, electrons, and ions of other elements are excluded.

Unlike [lithium_density_at_limiter](name:lithium_density_at_limiter), which
is evaluated at a limiter, this quantity is evaluated at the divertor-target
sheath entrance. It therefore represents the divertor-target member of the
lithium-density family rather than a limiter or general plasma-boundary
value.

items.name: radial_electron_velocity
items.description:
Signed projection of the local electron-fluid bulk flow onto the
major-radius direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The radial electron velocity is the major-radius component of the local
electron-fluid bulk flow in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame. Here $R$ is major radius measured from the toroidal symmetry axis,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It describes mean
translational motion of electrons rather than their random thermal motion.

The component is defined by projection:

$$
u_{eR} = \mathbf{u}_e \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $u_{eR}$ is the radial electron velocity, $\mathbf{u}_e$ is the local
[electron velocity](name:electron_velocity), and $\hat{R}$ is the unit
vector toward increasing major radius.

The bulk flow is the mean over the electron velocity distribution at the
same location; it is not a mass-weighted mean over all plasma species. This
quantity is a signed component, not the magnitude of the electron bulk
velocity. The major-radius direction does not generally coincide with the
normal to a magnetic flux surface or with a direction perpendicular to the
magnetic field.

Like [toroidal electron velocity](name:toroidal_electron_velocity), it is a
directional projection of the same electron-fluid velocity vector, rather
than a separate flow contribution.

Sign convention: Positive when the electron bulk flow has a component toward
increasing major radius, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

items.name: boron_density_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Boron ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal, summed over
all boron ionization states and excluding neutral boron.
items.documentation:
Boron ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the local
concentration of boron ions at the inner shoulder of the H-mode transport
barrier, summed over all positive ionization states.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{B}} = \sum_{z=1}^{5} n_{\mathrm{B}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{B}}$ is the total boron ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{B}^{z+}}$ is the number density of boron ions with charge state
$z+$, and $z$ is the positive integer ionization state from one through
five.

This quantity applies locally to boron ions at the pedestal top, whose
position is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is
summed over all boron ion charge states, excludes neutral boron, and is
neither line-averaged nor volume-averaged.

It is the boron-specific component of the broader [density at the pedestal
top](name:density_at_pedestal_top). Unlike [electron density at the pedestal
top](name:electron_density_at_pedestal_top), it counts boron ions rather
than electrons; unlike [boron density at the
limiter](name:boron_density_at_limiter), it is evaluated at the pedestal-top
locus.

items.name: surface_area_of_divertor_tile
items.description:
Geometric area of the plasma-facing surface of an individual divertor tile,
defining the surface over which incident plasma loads are spatially
integrated.
items.documentation:
The tile surface area is the geometric area of the plasma-facing wetted
surface of one individual divertor tile. It is a property of the tile
geometry, independent of the incident heat, particle, or current load.

The area is defined by

$$
A_{\rm tile} = \int_{S_{\rm tile}} dA
$$

where $S_{\rm tile}$ is the plasma-facing tile surface and $dA$ is an
elemental surface area. The result provides the geometric denominator for
converting an integrated load into a tile-averaged surface density, such as
the [energy flux at a divertor target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target).

This quantity applies to one tile and must not be confused with the [wetted
area of a divertor target](name:wetted_area_of_divertor_target), which
characterizes a target-level deposited-flux region, or the total wetted area
of the divertor summed over multiple targets.

items.name: counter_passing_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Flux-surface-averaged Coulomb-collisional power transferred from
counter-passing nonthermal particles to thermal ions of a specified species,
summed over all ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Counter-passing thermal-ion collisional power density is the signed
volumetric rate of kinetic-energy transfer from counter-passing nonthermal
particles to thermal ions of a specified species, averaged over a magnetic
flux surface. Counter-passing particles follow passing guiding-center orbits
whose transit is opposite to the reference co-passing direction. This orbit
restriction selects the nonthermal source distribution, not the thermal-ion
recipient orbits.

For nonthermal source species $a$ and recipient ion species $i$, the
contribution is defined by the recipient kinetic-energy moment of the
Coulomb collision operator:

$$
P_{i,\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \left\langle \sum_q \int \frac{1}{2}m_i v^2 C_{iq,a}[f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}},f_a^{\mathrm{counter}}] \, d^3v \right\rangle
$$

where $P_{i,\mathrm{counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the counter-passing
thermal-ion collisional power density, $q$ labels the recipient's ionic
charge states, $m_i$ is the recipient-ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is
recipient-ion velocity, and $v=|\mathbf{v}|$ is its speed. The function
$f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal-ion velocity distribution for charge
state $q$, and $f_a^{\mathrm{counter}}$ is the counter-passing portion of
the nonthermal source distribution. The operator $C_{iq,a}$ gives the
collisional time derivative of the recipient distribution due to that
source. The integral covers all recipient-ion velocities, and angle brackets
denote the magnetic-flux-surface average weighted by the volume element
between neighboring flux surfaces.

The charge-state sum includes all ionic charge states of the specified
recipient species, not all ion species. The recipients are thermal ions,
excluding fast-ion recipients; the quantity is their collisional energy
source or sink, not their stored energy. In contrast, [charge-state-resolved
thermal-ion collisional power
density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions)
retains one specified ionic charge state.

This quantity is the counter-passing contribution to the flux-surface
average of [thermal-ion collisional power
density](name:thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions). Adding the
corresponding [co-passing
contribution](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions)
and trapped contribution, with the same averaging convention, recovers that
orbit-summed average.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer net kinetic
energy to the thermal-ion recipients from the counter-passing nonthermal
population.

items.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Poloidal component of the effective advective velocity transporting momentum
for a single neutral species internal state in edge-plasma transport,
distinct from bulk particle flow; it lies in the poloidal direction of the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The poloidal component of the [neutral internal-state momentum convection
velocity](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection)
is the effective advective velocity for poloidal momentum transport of a
single neutral species internal state in edge-plasma fluid transport,
distinct from bulk particle flow. The poloidal direction lies in the $R$-$Z$
plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The component is defined by projecting the effective momentum-convection
velocity onto the local poloidal unit vector:

$$
V_{\mathrm{mom},\mathrm{pol}}^{(n,\alpha)} = \mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{mom}}^{(n,\alpha)} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{pol}}
$$

where $\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{mom}}^{(n,\alpha)}$ is the effective
momentum-convection velocity for neutral species $n$ in internal state
$\alpha$, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the local poloidal unit
vector, and $V_{\mathrm{mom},\mathrm{pol}}^{(n,\alpha)}$ is the resulting
component.

This quantity represents momentum-transport advection rather than neutral
center-of-mass or particle-flow velocity. The [vertical neutral
internal-state momentum convection
velocity](name:vertical_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity)
provides the complementary cylindrical projection, while the [poloidal
neutral state momentum convection
velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_state_momentum_convection_velocity) does not
express the explicit internal-state resolution retained here.

Sign convention: Positive when the projected velocity points in the
direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $\theta$ the poloidal angle of the
adopted flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$.

items.name: toroidal_linear_mhd_mode_reference_phase
items.description:
Signed angular offset that fixes the complex phase of a linear MHD
perturbation’s toroidal Fourier mode relative to its zero-phase reference.
items.documentation:
The reference phase is the angular offset assigned to the complex
eigenfunction of a linear MHD perturbation with a specified toroidal
harmonic. It fixes the mode’s phase origin and is not a spatial displacement
or amplitude.

Using the complex-amplitude convention, the toroidal dependence of a
perturbation quantity is written as:

$$
\widetilde{Q}(R,Z,\phi)=\widehat{Q}(R,Z)\exp\!\left[i\left(n\phi+\phi_{\mathrm{ref}}\right)\right]
$$

where $\widetilde{Q}$ is the complex perturbation, $\widehat{Q}$ is its
complex amplitude, $n$ is the dimensionless integer toroidal mode number,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $\phi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reference phase.
$R$ and $Z$ are the major-radius and vertical coordinates in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The toroidal harmonic is
identified by mode number, while its phase is carried by quantities such as
the [toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic
field](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field).

The reference phase does not specify perturbation amplitude, growth rate,
oscillation frequency, or temporal phase.

Sign convention: Positive when the complex mode phase advances in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
items.description:
Outgoing energy flux per unit plasma-facing wall area produced when incident
plasma ions recombine at the surface, restricted to the ion-associated
channel and summed over incident-ion species and charge states.
items.documentation:
Ion energy flux at the wall due to recombination quantifies the rate at
which recombination-associated energy from incident plasma ions leaves a
plasma-facing surface per unit area. It is the ion-associated component
summed over incident-ion species and charge states, not the incident plasma
energy flux or energy deposited in the wall material.

The aggregate is defined from charge-state-resolved components by:

$$
Q_{\mathrm{rec,ion}}(\mathbf{x}_w) = \sum_{s,q} Q_{\mathrm{rec},s,q}(\mathbf{x}_w)
$$

where $\mathbf{x}_w$ is the wall location, $s$ identifies an incident-ion
species, $q$ identifies its charge state, and $Q_{\mathrm{rec},s,q}$ is the
corresponding [ion charge-state energy flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:ion_charge_state_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).
The sum includes all represented incident-ion species and charge states.

As a component of [energy flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination), this quantity
retains only the ion-associated energy channel. Unlike particle flux at the
wall due to recombination, it weights the outgoing recombination
contribution by carried energy; it is distinct from incident [ion kinetic
energy flux at the wall](name:ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall).

items.name: toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Density-weighted tungsten impurity-ion bulk-flow velocity along increasing
toroidal angle, averaged over all ionization charge states at the internal
transport barrier.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local toroidal component of the tungsten impurity-ion
bulk-flow velocity at the internal transport barrier, with contributions
from ionic charge states combined by density weighting.

The charge-state-averaged velocity is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{W}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{W}^{q+}}\left(\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{W}^{q+}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}\right)}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{W}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ is the tungsten ionic charge state, $n_{\mathrm{W}^{q+}}$ is its
number density, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{W}^{q+}}$ is its bulk-flow velocity,
and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The sum includes all tungsten
ionization charge states and excludes neutral tungsten. The corresponding
[toroidal tungsten velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) differs only by its
spatial locus, while [toroidal iron velocity at the internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier)
illustrates the analogous charge-state-averaged quantity for another
impurity species.

Sign convention: Positive when the tungsten-ion flow points in the direction
of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: ion_charge_state_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
items.description:
Kinetic-energy power flux density carried by ions in a specified charge
state leaving a plasma-facing surface through sputtering, reflection, or
related surface-emission processes.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the outward kinetic-energy flux density carried by ions in
a specified species and charge state emitted from a plasma-facing surface
through sputtering, reflection, or related surface-emission processes.

The charge-state-resolved kinetic-energy flux density is defined by

$$
q_{\mathrm{kin},s} = \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{n}>0} \frac{1}{2}m_s v^2\,(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{n}) f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $s$ identifies the selected ion species and charge state, $m_s$ is its
particle mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $v=|\mathbf{v}|$,
$\mathbf{n}$ is the outward surface-normal unit vector, and $f_s$ is its
emitted-particle velocity distribution. The outward condition excludes
particles incident on the surface.

This is one charge-state contribution to [kinetic-energy flux at wall due to
surface emission](name:kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission),
excluding other ion charge states, electrons, particle potential energy,
photons, and other radiative energy. The ion-aggregated quantity [ion
kinetic-energy flux at wall due to surface
emission](name:ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission) sums
this contribution over ion species and charge states.

items.name: carbon_density_at_limiter
items.description:
Carbon ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a
plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all carbon ionization states and
excluding neutral carbon atoms.
items.documentation:
Carbon density at a limiter is the local number density of carbon ions in
the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface.
The evaluation point is the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath
entrance, consistent with the parent
[density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter) framework. Carbon supports six
ionization states ($\text{C}^{1+}$ through $\text{C}^{6+}$), and this
quantity sums over all of them; neutral carbon atoms are excluded from this
count.

The total charge-state-summed carbon density at the limiter is:

$$
n_\text{C} = \sum_{z=1}^{6} n_{\text{C}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\text{C}^{z+}}$ is the number density of carbon ions in charge
state $z$ at the limiter evaluation point.

Carbon enters the edge plasma primarily through physical sputtering,
chemical erosion, and recycling from carbon-based plasma-facing components.
The density is inferred from spectroscopic line emission (C II through C VI)
analyzed with collisional-radiative models that convert observed photon
emissivities to charge-state-resolved densities.

In carbon-wall configurations, $n_\text{C}$ at the limiter spans
approximately $10^{15}$–$10^{18}$ m$^{-3}$, depending on the carbon source
rate, local electron temperature, and scrape-off-layer plasma density.
Carbon impurities contribute to
[effective_charge_at_limiter](name:effective_charge_at_limiter) and radiate
strongly at edge electron temperatures of 10–100 eV. Analogous carbon
densities at other boundary locations are tracked by
[carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary)
and
[carbon_density_at_divertor_target](name:carbon_density_at_divertor_target).

items.name: thermal_particle_power_density_due_to_thermalization
items.description:
Local volumetric heating rate delivered to thermal particles when fast or
suprathermal particles lose kinetic energy through Coulomb thermalization.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the thermal-particle component of particle power density
due to thermalization: the local rate at which Coulomb collisions transfer
kinetic energy from a fast or suprathermal population to the specified
thermal population.

$$
q_{\mathrm{th}}=\left.\frac{\partial u_{\mathrm{th}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{Coulomb\ thermalization}}
$$

where $q_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the transferred power density, in W m$^{-3}$, and
$u_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal population's kinetic-energy density. The
derivative includes only energy exchange attributable to collisional
relaxation toward thermal equilibrium; it excludes direct injection, wave
heating, radiation, and other non-thermalization sources. Positive values
represent net energy gain by the thermal population.

items.name: fast_particle_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons
items.description:
Local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer per unit volume delivered to
fast particles by Coulomb collisions with background electrons, excluding
the reaction torque on electrons.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the local torque-density vector transferred to the
fast-particle population through Coulomb collisions with background
electrons. It represents angular-momentum exchange received by fast
particles, rather than the equal-and-opposite reaction torque assigned to
electrons.

The local collisional angular-momentum balance is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{fp}\leftarrow e}^{\mathrm{C}}
=
\left.\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}_{\mathrm{fp}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{C},e}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{fp}\leftarrow e}^{\mathrm{C}}$ is the
torque-density vector received by fast particles from electrons,
$\boldsymbol{\ell}_{\mathrm{fp}}$ is the angular-momentum density of the
fast-particle population, $t$ is time, and the subscripts and superscript
identify Coulomb-collisional exchange from background electrons.

This quantity is local and retains the complete torque vector rather than
selecting a toroidal, poloidal, or radial component. Its recipient
population is the fast-particle population, its collision partner is the
background electron population, and its aggregation is over the
fast-particle population represented locally; it is not volume-integrated
and excludes the opposite reaction torque on electrons.

It is the fast-particle specialization of the broader [particle torque
density due to Coulomb collisions with
electrons](name:particle_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons),
while [toroidal fast-particle torque density due to Coulomb collisions with
electrons](name:toroidal_fast_particle_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons)
is the toroidal component-resolved instance of this vector quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when the relevant vector component points in the
corresponding increasing-coordinate direction of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

items.name: total_neutral_internal_state_pressure
items.description:
Kinetic pressure of all neutral particles in a specified internal quantum or
excitation state, combining thermal and nonthermal fast-neutral
contributions.
items.documentation:
The total neutral internal state pressure is the kinetic pressure associated
with all neutral particles in a specified internal quantum or excitation
state, combining thermal and nonthermal fast-neutral contributions. It is
the total-contribution specialization of [neutral internal state
pressure](name:neutral_internal_state_pressure).

For the aggregate velocity distribution in state $s$, the scalar pressure is
one-third of the pressure-tensor trace:

$$
p_s^{\mathrm{tot}} = \frac{1}{3}\int m_n \lvert\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_s\rvert^2 f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $m_n$ is the neutral-particle mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity,
$\mathbf{u}_s$ is the aggregate mean velocity, and $f_s$ is the distribution
of all neutral particles in state $s$. Subtracting the mean flow excludes
common bulk-flow dynamic pressure. Unlike [thermal neutral internal state
pressure](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure), this quantity
includes nonthermal fast-neutral contributions and does not require an
isotropic Maxwellian distribution. It remains restricted to the specified
internal state and therefore differs from [total neutral
pressure](name:total_neutral_pressure), which aggregates over internal
states.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_current_center
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate of the plasma-current centroid, obtained by
normalizing the toroidal-current first moment over the poloidal plasma
cross-section by total plasma current.
items.documentation:
The radial coordinate of the current center is the major-radius location of
the centroid of the toroidal plasma-current distribution. It identifies a
current-weighted position and is distinct from the geometric centroid or the
magnetic axis.

The coordinate is defined by the toroidal-current first moment:

$$
R_c = \frac{\displaystyle\int_{D_p} R\,j_\phi\,dS}{I_p}
$$

where $R_c$ is the major-radius coordinate of the current center, $R$ is the
major-radius coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, $j_\phi$ is the toroidal component of the plasma [current
density](name:current_density), $dS$ is an element of poloidal
cross-sectional area, $D_p$ is the plasma current-carrying poloidal
cross-section, and $I_p$ is the total toroidal plasma current, equal to the
corresponding integral of $j_\phi$ over $D_p$.

The quantity applies to the full plasma-current distribution and uses a
current-weighted first-moment aggregation over the poloidal cross-section.
It excludes weighting by particle density, pressure, magnetic-field
strength, or geometric area alone; the resulting position is therefore not a
generic geometric center.

This quantity is a locus-specific instance of the general [radial
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate), evaluated at the current center. Its
vertical counterpart, [vertical coordinate of the current
center](name:vertical_coordinate_of_current_center), supplies the
corresponding vertical position needed to locate the current centroid in the
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: total_particle_source_rate_of_divertor_due_to_recycling
items.description:
Total equivalent-electron rate of neutral and ion particles re-emitted from
all divertor surfaces into the plasma by recycling.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the aggregate particle source produced when neutral and ion
particles are re-emitted from divertor surfaces into the plasma by
recycling.

The defining rate is

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{rec}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{eq}}}{dt}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{rec}}$ is the total recycled particle source rate,
$N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the cumulative equivalent-electron count of re-emitted
particles, and $t$ is time.

The quantity covers all divertor surfaces and combines the neutral and ion
contributions using equivalent-electron counting. It is a total source rate
rather than a local surface flux density, and it excludes particle sources
produced by processes other than recycling or originating outside the
divertor.

This is a gross re-emission rate and does not by itself represent the net
particle balance after incident-particle losses. Unlike [power of the
divertor due to recombination](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination),
it counts recycled particles without weighting them by deposited energy.

items.name: argon_density
items.description:
Charge-state-summed number density of argon ions, including Ar+ through
Ar18+ and excluding neutral argon; local and averaged forms share this
definition.
items.documentation:
Argon density is the number of argon ions per unit volume, summed over all
ionization stages from singly charged Ar+ through fully stripped Ar18+.
Neutral argon is excluded.

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ar}} = \sum_{Z=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{Z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the total argon-ion number density, $Z$ is the
integer argon charge state, and $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{Z+}}$ is the number density
of argon ions in that charge state.

The definition applies to a local value and to averages over a specified
chord or confined plasma volume, including the [line-averaged argon
density](name:line_averaged_argon_density) and [volume-averaged argon
density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density). It is distinct from argon
count, which represents an equivalent-electron inventory rather than
particles per volume.

items.name: current_density_due_to_ion_inertia
items.description:
Vector current density arising from the inertial force terms of the ion
fluid in the two-fluid plasma model, principally through the polarization
drift generated by ion acceleration in the momentum equation.
items.documentation:
The current density due to ion inertia represents the net electric current
produced by the inertial acceleration terms in the ion fluid momentum
equation. In a two-fluid plasma description, ions with finite mass
contribute to net charge transport whenever they are accelerated — through
flow convergence, curvature forces, or time-varying electric fields — giving
rise to a polarization-type current that is absent in the massless-electron
fluid.

The dominant contribution is the ion polarization drift current:

$$
\mathbf{J}_{inertia} = \frac{m_i n_i}{e B^2} \mathbf{B} \times \frac{d_i \mathbf{v}_{\perp i}}{dt}
$$

where $m_i$ is the ion mass, $n_i$ is the ion number density, $e$ is the
elementary charge, $B$ is the magnetic field magnitude, and $d_i/dt =
\partial/\partial t + \mathbf{v}_i \cdot \nabla$ is the ion convective
derivative applied to the perpendicular ion velocity $\mathbf{v}_{\perp i}$.

The divergence of this current feeds the vorticity equation and contributes
to the radial current balance, making it particularly significant in edge
and scrape-off-layer transport modeling where large ion flows develop. In
multi-fluid transport codes, the vector is evaluated on generalized geometry
grids and decomposed into cylindrical components —
[radial_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia](name:radial_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia),
[toroidal_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia),
[vertical_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia](name:vertical_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia)
— and a field-aligned component
[parallel_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia).
The analogous turbulent contribution is given by
[current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport](name:current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport).

items.name: calibration_factor_of_visible_camera
items.description:
Multiplicative radiometric coefficient that converts a corrected
visible-camera detector signal into absolute photon radiance integrated over
the admitted spectral band.
items.documentation:
A visible-camera radiometric factor converts a consistently corrected
detector signal into band-integrated photon radiance. It represents the
combined response of the optical throughput, detector sensitivity, pixel
etendue, and exposure treatment rather than the radiance itself.

The defining conversion is

$$
L_{\mathrm{vis}} = C_{\mathrm{vis}} S_{\mathrm{corr}}
$$

where $L_{\mathrm{vis}}$ is the [visible-camera
brightness](name:brightness_of_visible_camera), $C_{\mathrm{vis}}$ is this
visible-camera factor, and $S_{\mathrm{corr}}$ is the corrected detector
signal. The spectral dependence is integrated over the relevant visible
passband. Unlike the resulting brightness, the factor is a calibration
coefficient and must be applied to the corrected signal; it is the
camera-specific component of the parent factor of visible camera.

items.name: poloidal_total_ion_energy_flux
items.description:
Poloidal total ion energy flux is the signed local energy-transfer rate per
area normal to the poloidal direction, summed over all ion species and ionic
charge states.
items.documentation:
Poloidal total ion energy flux is the signed projection of the aggregate ion
energy-flux vector onto the local poloidal direction. It includes conductive
thermal-energy transport and convective enthalpy or bulk-kinetic transport
carried by ions.

The defining projection and aggregation are:

$$
\Gamma_{W,i,\mathrm{p}} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W,i}\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}} = \sum_a\sum_z \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W,a,z}\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{W,i,\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal total ion energy flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W,i}$ is the [total ion energy-flux
vector](name:total_ion_energy_flux), and $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W,a,z}$ is
the energy-flux vector carried by ion species $a$ in ionic charge state $z$.
The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}}$ points toward increasing
local poloidal angle $\theta$ in a constant-toroidal-angle plane. In the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The geometric sense of
increasing $\theta$ is set by the specified poloidal-angle convention.

The sum includes all ion species and all their ionic charge states, without
density weighting; electron and neutral energy fluxes are excluded. Each
species contribution, summed over its ionic charge states, is a [poloidal
ion energy flux](name:poloidal_ion_energy_flux). This quantity is a local
flux density, not a surface-integrated power or a flux-surface average. Its
geometric poloidal projection is distinct from the magnetic-field projection
defining [parallel total ion energy
flux](name:parallel_total_ion_energy_flux).

Sign convention: Positive when net ion energy is transported toward
increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

items.name: field_line_average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer
items.description:
Species-resolved temperature averaged by arc length along an open magnetic
field line between upstream and downstream locations in the scrape-off
layer.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the temperature of a specified plasma species averaged
along an open magnetic field line traversing the scrape-off layer. It
represents the common field-line-averaged quantity instantiated by the
electron and ion species-specific children.

The field-line average is defined by

$$
\overline{T}_{\sigma,\mathrm{FL}} = \frac{\int_{\ell_u}^{\ell_d} T_\sigma(\ell)\,d\ell}{\int_{\ell_u}^{\ell_d} d\ell}
$$

where $\overline{T}_{\sigma,\mathrm{FL}}$ is the field-line-averaged
temperature, $\sigma$ identifies the selected plasma species,
$T_\sigma(\ell)$ is its local temperature, and $\ell$ is arc length along
the open magnetic field line. The limits $\ell_u$ and $\ell_d$ identify the
upstream and downstream endpoints of the averaging interval.

The quantity applies to one species at a time and uses an arc-length average
along the open field line; it is neither a sum nor an average over multiple
species. It is restricted to the scrape-off layer and does not denote a
local temperature at one point or a volume average over that region.

This is the field-line-averaged, species-resolved specialization of [average
temperature over the scrape-off
layer](name:average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer). Its concrete
realizations include [electron field-line average temperature over the
scrape-off
layer](name:electron_field_line_average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer)
and [ion field-line average temperature over the scrape-off
layer](name:ion_field_line_average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer), which
differ only by the selected species.

items.name: halo_current
items.description:
Halo current in the halo plasma region during a disruption is the electric
current vector carried by the halo plasma on open magnetic field lines
between the last closed flux surface and the first wall. Its poloidal and
toroidal components are obtained by integrating the halo current density
over oriented cross sections of the halo region.
items.documentation:
Halo current in the halo plasma region during a disruption is the electric
current vector carried by the halo plasma flowing on open magnetic field
lines between the last closed flux surface and the first wall. It resolves
into a poloidal component and a toroidal component, each obtained by
integrating the halo current density over an oriented cross section of the
halo region.

The component currents are surface integrals of the halo current density,
and the current vector is their sum along the corresponding unit directions:

$$
\mathbf{I}_\mathrm{h} = I_{\mathrm{h},\theta}\,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta + I_{\mathrm{h},\phi}\,\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}, \qquad I_{\mathrm{h},a} = \int_{S_a} \mathbf{J}_\mathrm{h}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_a\,dS,\quad a\in\{\theta,\phi\}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_\mathrm{h}$ is the halo current density, $S_a$ is an
oriented cross section of the halo region with positive normal
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_a$, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$ is tangent to increasing
poloidal angle $\theta$, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is tangent to
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame. The poloidal angle $\theta$ is the angular coordinate in the
meridional plane of that $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame about the chosen magnetic-axis
reference and is distinct from the toroidal angle $\phi$.

The scalar coefficient $I_{\mathrm{h},\theta}$ is
[poloidal_halo_current](name:poloidal_halo_current) and
$I_{\mathrm{h},\phi}$ is
[toroidal_halo_current](name:toroidal_halo_current). This integrated current
vector is distinct from halo_current_density, the local field
$\mathbf{J}_\mathrm{h}$ prior to integration over $S_a$, and it counts only
current carried by the halo plasma itself, excluding current confined to
passive conducting structures after path closure outside the halo region.

Sign convention: Positive when the poloidal component is directed along
increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ and the toroidal component is directed
along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Poloidal neutral energy diffusion coefficient is the effective down-gradient
flux-gradient coefficient for diffusive transport of neutral-particle
thermal energy in the poloidal direction.
items.documentation:
Poloidal neutral energy diffusion coefficient is the scalar effective
transport coefficient for diffusive transport of neutral-particle thermal
energy in the poloidal direction. It characterizes only the poloidal
component of the neutral thermal-energy flux associated with gradients of
neutral thermal-energy density.

In a Fickian closure for the poloidal diffusive energy flux, it is the
coefficient $D^{\mathrm{pol}}_{E,n}$ in the flux-gradient relation:

$$
q^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,\mathrm{pol}} = -D^{\mathrm{pol}}_{E,n}\,\nabla_{\mathrm{pol}} w_{E,n}
$$

where $q^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal component of
the diffusive flux of neutral thermal energy, $D^{\mathrm{pol}}_{E,n}$ is
the poloidal neutral energy diffusion coefficient, $\nabla_{\mathrm{pol}}$
is the directional derivative along the poloidal direction, and $w_{E,n}$ is
the neutral thermal-energy density. The minus sign defines the down-gradient
closure: a positive coefficient gives a diffusive flux toward decreasing
$w_{E,n}$ along the poloidal direction.

The scope is edge-plasma transport of neutral particles represented by one
effective coefficient for the aggregate neutral population. It is not
resolved by neutral internal state, is not an ion charge-state-resolved
quantity, and excludes charged-particle transport. The energy qualifier
denotes thermal energy carried by neutrals; it excludes particle-number
diffusion, momentum diffusion, radiative loss terms, source terms, and
convective energy flux.

This quantity is the poloidal member of [neutral energy diffusion
coefficient](name:neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and is directionally
distinct from [parallel neutral energy diffusion
coefficient](name:parallel_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient). It is
closely related to [poloidal neutral energy
diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusivity), but this name
specifically denotes the coefficient in the neutral thermal-energy-density
flux-gradient law above. The internal-state-resolved counterpart is
[poloidal neutral internal-state energy diffusion
coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient),
which applies to a specified neutral internal state rather than to the
aggregate neutral population; the analogous internal-state diffusivity is
[poloidal neutral internal-state energy
diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity).

items.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_minimum_absolute_safety_factor
items.description:
Dimensionless magnetic-surface label giving the normalized toroidal flux at
the closed surface where the magnitude of the safety factor reaches its
minimum.
items.documentation:
This quantity identifies the nested closed magnetic surface on which the
magnitude of the safety factor is minimized, using the normalized toroidal
magnetic-flux coordinate of that surface.

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}} = \sqrt{\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ is the normalized toroidal-flux coordinate,
$\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the
evaluated surface, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}$ is its value at the magnetic
axis, and $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}}$ is its value at the equilibrium
boundary.

The value is a single equilibrium coordinate evaluated at the surface of
minimum safety-factor magnitude; it is not a flux-surface profile, an
average over surfaces, or the minimum safety-factor value itself. It is
distinct from a cylindrical radial distance and from a local vector
component. The parent [normalized toroidal flux
coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate) supplies the
coordinate definition, while [normalized poloidal flux coordinate at minimum
absolute safety
factor](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_at_minimum_absolute_safety_factor)
gives the analogous poloidal-flux label at the same physical locus.

items.name: parallel_ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Parallel directional diffusion coefficient governing down-gradient transport
of bulk-ion momentum along the local magnetic-field direction in a
magnetized plasma.
items.documentation:
The parallel ion momentum diffusion coefficient is the parallel directional
component of the [ion momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) vector. It
parameterizes down-gradient diffusion of bulk-ion momentum along the local
magnetic-field direction, distinct from radial and poloidal transport
components.

In a gradient-diffusion closure, its constitutive relation is:

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel,\mathrm{mom}}=-\chi_{\parallel,\mathrm{mom}}\nabla_{\parallel}(m_i n_i v_{i,\parallel})
$$

where $\Gamma_{\parallel,\mathrm{mom}}$ is the diffusive parallel flux
density of ion momentum, $\chi_{\parallel,\mathrm{mom}}$ is this
coefficient, $\nabla_{\parallel}$ is the derivative along the local magnetic
field, $m_i$ is the ion mass, $n_i$ is the ion number density, and
$v_{i,\parallel}$ is the parallel bulk-ion flow velocity. The coefficient
describes parallel momentum diffusion only; it is not the momentum flux
itself and does not represent cross-field transport. The species-agnostic
[parallel momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:parallel_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) and the
directionally distinct toroidal ion momentum diffusion coefficient define
related but broader or differently projected quantities.

items.name: line_averaged_electron_temperature
items.description:
Thermal energy of the bulk electron population expressed as an
energy-equivalent temperature, averaged along a plasma chord.
items.documentation:
Line-averaged electron temperature is the energy-equivalent measure of the
mean random kinetic energy of the bulk electron population, averaged along a
plasma chord.

The defining path-length average is:

$$
T_{e,\mathrm{line}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L T_e(l)\,dl
$$

where $T_{e,\mathrm{line}}$ is the line-averaged electron temperature,
$T_e(l)$ is the local [electron temperature](name:electron_temperature) at
path coordinate $l$, and $L$ is the total chord length. The coordinate $l$
measures distance along the specified plasma chord, and the averaging is
uniform with respect to path length.

This is an intensive quantity for the bulk electron population, aggregated
along the chord rather than summed over electron energies or particle
populations. It excludes ion temperatures and differs from the local
electron temperature because it combines values along the entire chord.

The line average is a chord-integrated representation of the parent
[electron_temperature](name:electron_temperature), whereas
[volume_averaged_electron_temperature](name:volume_averaged_electron_temperature)
applies a volume average over the confined plasma and is therefore a
distinct spatial aggregation.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_polarizer
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate of the polarizer’s geometric reference point, namely
its circular center or local-plane origin, measured from the toroidal
symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the major-radius location of a polarizer’s geometric
reference point. This point is the center for a circular polarizer or the
origin of the local coordinate system describing a planar polarizer.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the coordinate is
defined from the point’s horizontal Cartesian coordinates by

$$
R_{\mathrm{pol}} = \sqrt{x_{\mathrm{pol}}^2+y_{\mathrm{pol}}^2}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the polarizer reference point’s major-radius
coordinate, and $x_{\mathrm{pol}}$ and $y_{\mathrm{pol}}$ are its horizontal
coordinates in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis.
Here $R$ denotes major radius, $\phi$ denotes toroidal angle, and $Z$
denotes vertical height.

The quantity applies only to the polarizer reference point and is
nonnegative; it is not the radial coordinate of an arbitrary point on the
polarizer surface and is not a flux-surface-normal projection. It is the
polarizer-specific realization of the general [radial
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate).

Together with the [toroidal coordinate of the
polarizer](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_polarizer), this coordinate locates
the same geometric reference point in the cylindrical frame.

items.name: parallel_total_fast_ion_pressure
items.description:
Total fast-ion parallel pressure, summed over all fast-ion species and
charge states, is the gyrotropic stress component along the local magnetic
field.
items.documentation:
The parallel total fast-ion pressure is the principal field-aligned
component of the gyrotropic pressure tensor of suprathermal ions, summed
over all fast-ion species and charge states. It is one of the two
independent components that determine the anisotropic pressure represented
by [total fast-ion pressure](name:total_fast_ion_pressure).

It is defined by the projection

$$
P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}} = \hat{\mathbf b} \cdot \overleftrightarrow{\mathbf P}_{\mathrm{fast}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf b}
$$

where $P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the parallel pressure component,
$\overleftrightarrow{\mathbf P}_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the total fast-ion
pressure tensor, and $\hat{\mathbf b} = \mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ is the unit
vector along the local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf B$. The complementary
[perpendicular total fast-ion
pressure](name:perpendicular_total_fast_ion_pressure) describes stress
transverse to the field; equality of the two components corresponds to an
isotropic fast-ion pressure.

items.name: line_averaged_effective_charge
items.description:
Effective charge of a plasma ion mixture averaged uniformly along a
specified line of sight, expressing its chord-mean composition factor for
electron–ion Coulomb scattering.
items.documentation:
Effective charge averaged along a specified plasma line of sight describes
the chord-mean charge-state composition of the ion mixture relevant to
electron–ion Coulomb scattering.

The line average is defined by:

$$
\bar{Z}_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L Z_{\mathrm{eff}}\,dl
$$

where $\bar{Z}_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the line-averaged effective charge,
$Z_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the local [effective charge](name:effective_charge),
$L$ is the length of the specified plasma chord, and $l$ is distance along
that chord.

The local composition factor is $Z_{\mathrm{eff}} = \sum_a n_a Z_a^2/n_e$,
where $a$ indexes all ion species and their ionized charge states, $n_a$ is
the number density of each ionic population, $Z_a$ is its charge number, and
$n_e$ is the free-electron number density. The mixture includes both fuel
and impurity ions; it is not the mean charge number of a selected species.

The averaging uses uniform length weighting of the local effective charge.
It is distinct from an unnormalized chord integral, an emissivity-weighted
average, or a ratio formed from separately chord-integrated charge moments.

items.name: upper_bound_energy_of_detector_pixel
items.description:
The upper bound energy of a detector pixel is the maximum photon energy at
the high-energy edge of its spectral bandpass in an X-ray crystal
spectrometer.
items.documentation:
The upper bound energy of a detector pixel is the maximum photon energy at
the high-energy edge of the spectral interval accepted by that pixel in an
X-ray crystal spectrometer. It defines the upper endpoint of the
pixel-specific photon-energy bandpass.

This quantity applies to one detector pixel and describes its individual
spectral acceptance interval; it is not an energy averaged over pixels or
over the full spectrometer. It is distinct from the representative [energy
of a detector pixel](name:energy_of_detector_pixel), which identifies the
central or calibrated spectral-channel energy, and from the [lower bound
energy of a detector pixel](name:lower_bound_energy_of_detector_pixel),
which defines the lower endpoint of the same interval.

Together, the upper and lower bounds delimit the photon-energy range
accepted by each pixel, while the representative pixel energy identifies the
spectral-channel assignment within that range.

items.name: effective_charge_at_limiter
items.description:
Effective charge number of the local ion mixture in boundary plasma
immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface.
items.documentation:
The effective charge at a limiter quantifies the charge-squared-weighted
composition of the local positive-ion mixture immediately adjacent to the
plasma-facing limiter surface. It is the limiter-local specialization of
charge_at_limiter.

$$
Z_\mathrm{eff} = \frac{\sum_i n_i Z_i^2}{\sum_i n_i Z_i}
$$

where $Z_\mathrm{eff}$ is the effective charge number, $n_i$ is the number
density of ion population $i$ in m$^{-3}$, and $Z_i$ is its positive integer
charge number. The sum includes positive ion species and charge states,
while neutral atoms are excluded. A pure hydrogenic ion mixture gives
$Z_\mathrm{eff}=1$; admixture of multiply charged impurity ions raises the
value. The limiter location distinguishes this quantity from
[effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary](name:effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary),
which is evaluated at the plasma boundary.

items.name: particle_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons
items.description:
Local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer per unit volume delivered to
a specified particle population by Coulomb collisions with electrons.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local vector torque density delivered to a specified
recipient particle population by Coulomb collisions with electrons. It
represents angular-momentum transfer to that population and excludes the
equal-and-opposite reaction torque assigned to the electrons.

For a local collisional force density, the torque density is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{a\leftarrow e}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{r}) = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{a\leftarrow e}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{r})
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{a\leftarrow e}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the
torque-density vector transferred to recipient population $a$, $\mathbf{r}$
is the displacement from the torque origin to the local volume element, and
$\mathbf{f}_{a\leftarrow e}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the Coulomb-collisional
force density transferred from electrons $e$ to population $a$.

The quantity is local, resolved for the receiving particle population, and
restricted to Coulomb collisions with electrons; it is not volume-integrated
and is not summed over other receiving populations or collision partners.
Non-Coulomb forces, energy-transfer rates, and the opposite reaction torque
on electrons are excluded. The [fast-particle torque-density
instance](name:fast_particle_torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons)
applies this shared definition to fast particles.

This is the population-resolved vector specialization of [torque density due
to Coulomb collisions with
electrons](name:torque_density_due_to_coulomb_collisions_with_electrons).
Its vector components retain the directional information of the collisional
angular-momentum transfer, while any component or aggregate defined
