elsewhere is a derived restriction of this vector quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when a reported torque-density component points
along the corresponding positive basis direction of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Dimensionless vertical ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient
that scales the free-streaming bound on vertical momentum transport for a
specified ion charge state.
items.documentation:
The vertical ion charge-state momentum coefficient is a dimensionless
flux-limiter parameter for momentum transport of a specified ion charge
state in the vertical $Z$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame. It is the vertical component of the vector quantity [ion
charge-state momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

The coefficient $\alpha_{s,Z}$ bounds the vertical momentum-flux density
through the harmonic-mean combination:

$$
\Pi_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\alpha_{s,Z} \, \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}} \, \Pi_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{diff}}}{|\Pi_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{diff}}| + \alpha_{s,Z} \, \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

where $\Pi_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited vertical momentum-flux
density for ion charge state $s$, $\Pi_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the
collisional diffusive estimate of that vertical momentum-flux density, and
$\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}} = m_s n_s v_{\mathrm{th},s}^2$ is the free-streaming
reference scale with $m_s$ the ion mass, $n_s$ the charge-state number
density, and $v_{\mathrm{th},s}$ the thermal speed. When
$|\Pi_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{diff}}| \gg \alpha_{s,Z}\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}$, the
vertical flux saturates at $\pm\alpha_{s,Z}\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}$; otherwise
the diffusive value is recovered unchanged.

The coefficient is specific to the vertical component and is distinct from
the
[parallel](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
[poloidal](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
and
[toroidal](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient)
ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter coefficients. The neutral-particle
analog is
[neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).
The coefficient is intrinsically non-negative.

items.name: vertical_width_of_beamlet_group
items.description:
Full vertical cross-sectional extent of a neutral-beam-injection beamlet
group at the injection unit’s source surface.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the full vertical geometric width occupied collectively by
the beamlets in a neutral-beam-injection group at the injection unit’s
grounded-grid source surface.

The width is defined by the separation of the uppermost and lowermost
beamlet-group boundaries:

$$
w_v = Z_{\mathrm{top}} - Z_{\mathrm{bottom}}
$$

where $w_v$ is the vertical beamlet-group width, $Z_{\mathrm{top}}$ and
$Z_{\mathrm{bottom}}$ are the upper and lower vertical coordinates of the
group boundary, and $Z$ is the vertical coordinate in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame; $R$ is major radius and $\phi$ is toroidal
angle.

This quantity applies to the aggregate cross-sectional envelope of the
beamlet group at the source surface, not to an individual beamlet. It
represents the full width rather than a half-width, local spread, or width
evaluated at another position along the beam line.

The width changes along the beam line as the beamlets converge. It is
therefore distinct from the [vertical focal length of the beamlet
group](name:vertical_focal_length_of_beamlet_group), which is the distance
to the point of minimum vertical width rather than the width itself.

items.name: rate_due_to_beam_beam_fusion
items.description:
Global volume-integrated rate of fusion events or reaction-product
generation attributable to fusion between two nonthermal fuel-ion
populations supplied by neutral beams.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the global rate of beam-beam fusion events or of production
of a specified reaction product caused by collisions between two nonthermal
fuel-ion populations originating from beam injection. It is a
reaction-source quantity, not a local source density or directional flux.

The global rate is the volume integral of the local beam-beam fusion source
rate:

$$
\dot{N}_X = \int_V S_X^{\mathrm{BB}}(\mathbf{r})\,d^3\mathbf{r}
$$

where $\dot{N}_X$ is the global rate for counted entity $X$, $X$ denotes
either a fusion event or a specified reaction product, $V$ is the plasma
volume over which beam-beam reactions occur, $S_X^{\mathrm{BB}}(\mathbf{r})$
is the corresponding local source rate density, and $\mathbf{r}$ is
position.

The quantity aggregates the volume-integrated contribution from all
represented beam-beam fuel-ion reaction channels and, when a product is
specified, applies the corresponding product yield. Both reacting fuel-ion
populations are nonthermal beam-origin populations; the generic quantity
does not select a particular isotope pair, charge state, reaction product,
or product channel. It excludes beam-thermal and thermal-thermal fusion
contributions, as well as local source densities and surface or directional
fluxes.

The [neutron rate due to beam-beam
fusion](name:neutron_rate_due_to_beam_beam_fusion) is a product-specific
specialization that counts neutrons while retaining the same global volume
integration and beam-beam channel aggregation. The [source rate due to
beam-beam fusion](name:source_rate_due_to_beam_beam_fusion) represents the
corresponding product-resolved source-rate family, whereas [rate due to
beam-thermal fusion](name:rate_due_to_beam_thermal_fusion) uses one
beam-origin and one thermal reacting population and is therefore a distinct
fusion mechanism.

items.name: parallel_diamagnetic_current_density
items.description:
Parallel component of the diamagnetic current density, obtained by
projecting the magnetic-field–pressure-gradient drift current onto the local
magnetic-field direction.
items.documentation:
The parallel diamagnetic current density is the projection of the total
[diamagnetic current density](name:diamagnetic_current_density) onto the
local magnetic-field direction. It arises from the
magnetic-field–pressure-gradient drift current and represents the signed
field-aligned component of [current density due to diamagnetic
drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).

The projection is defined by:

$$
j_{\mathrm{dia},\parallel} = \hat{\mathbf{b}}\cdot\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{dia},\parallel}$ is the parallel diamagnetic current
density, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/B$ is the unit vector in the local
magnetic-field direction, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector,
$B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is the magnetic-field magnitude, and
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the [current density due to diamagnetic
drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).

This quantity applies to the total included edge-plasma current density
carried by all included charge carriers; it is not species- or
charge-state-resolved unless those qualifiers are part of the standard name.
It is a signed component, not the scalar magnitude [diamagnetic current
density](name:diamagnetic_current_density), and not a perpendicular
component with respect to the magnetic-field direction.

It is distinct from signed cylindrical projections such as [radial
diamagnetic current density](name:radial_diamagnetic_current_density),
[vertical diamagnetic current
density](name:vertical_diamagnetic_current_density), and toroidal
diamagnetic current density. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height, radial, toroidal, and vertical projections are along
$(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ respectively; the parallel projection is
along $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, not along any fixed cylindrical basis vector.

The same resolved contribution is denoted by [parallel current density due
to diamagnetic
drift](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) when
expressed as a contribution to [current density](name:current_density). For
the ideal isotropic scalar-pressure relation
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}=\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p/B^2$, where $p$ is total
scalar plasma pressure and $\nabla p$ is its spatial gradient,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is perpendicular to $\mathbf{B}$ and therefore
$j_{\mathrm{dia},\parallel}=0$; this is distinct from return-current
contributions such as [Pfirsch-Schlüter current
density](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density).

Sign convention: Positive when the diamagnetic current-density vector has a
component in the local magnetic-field direction $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$.

items.name: current_due_to_neutral_beam_injection
items.description:
Net toroidal plasma current driven by neutral-beam injection, combining the
fast-ion current and collisional electron return current after beam
ionization.
items.documentation:
Neutral-beam-driven plasma current is the net toroidal current produced when
injected neutrals ionize and their fast ions transfer momentum to the
plasma. It includes both the directed fast-ion contribution and the
associated collisional electron return-current contribution.

The current is defined by integrating the net neutral-beam-driven toroidal
current density over the plasma cross-sectional area:

$$
I_{\mathrm{NBI}} = \int_{\mathcal{A}_{p}} j_{\phi,\mathrm{NBI}}(R,Z)\,d\mathcal{A}
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{NBI}}$ is the neutral-beam-driven plasma current,
$j_{\phi,\mathrm{NBI}}$ is its toroidal current-density contribution, and
$\mathcal{A}_{p}$ is the plasma cross-sectional area in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

This source contribution is distinct from absorbed power of a neutral beam
injector and is combined with other current sources, including plasma
current due to ohmic induction and [current due to electron-cyclotron
current drive](name:current_due_to_electron_cyclotron_current_drive).

Sign convention: Positive when the net toroidal current flows in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: surface_area_of_neutron_detector
items.description:
Geometric area of the neutron-sensitive detector surface, excluding passive
housing, shielding, supports, electronics, projection effects, and
solid-angle weighting.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the geometric area of the neutron-sensitive active surface
of the detector. It includes the physical sensitive face, including
contributions from segmented or curved surfaces, and excludes passive
detector structures.

The area is defined by integration over the neutron-sensitive surface:

$$
A = \int_{S_{\rm active}} dS
$$

where $S_{\rm active}$ is the neutron-sensitive surface and $dS$ is an
element of geometric surface area. This is the active-surface component
represented by area of neutron detector; it is not an effective area
weighted by detection efficiency, neutron incidence angle, projection, or
solid angle.

items.name: ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude
items.description:
Ratio of the square of the toroidal-flux-coordinate gradient magnitude to
the square of the local magnetic-field magnitude. It is the unaveraged
magnetic-geometry ratio whose flux-surface average defines the corresponding
averaged geometry coefficient.
items.documentation:
Ratio of the square of the toroidal-flux-coordinate gradient magnitude to
the square of the local magnetic-field magnitude is a local scalar
magnetic-geometry coefficient. It expresses how the spatial metric of the
toroidal flux coordinate is weighted by the magnetic-field strength at the
same position.

The coefficient $K_{\rho B}$ is defined pointwise by:

$$
K_{\rho B}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{|\nabla \rho_\mathrm{tor}(\mathbf{x})|^2}{|\mathbf{B}(\mathbf{x})|^2}
$$

where $K_{\rho B}$ is this ratio, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position,
$\rho_\mathrm{tor}$ is the toroidal flux coordinate, $\nabla
\rho_\mathrm{tor}$ is its spatial gradient, $\mathbf{B}$ is the
magnetic-field vector, and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is the [magnetic-field
magnitude](name:magnetic_field_magnitude).

This quantity is the unaveraged, pointwise ratio evaluated where the
toroidal flux coordinate is differentiable and the magnetic-field magnitude
is nonzero. It does not include a flux-surface, volume, or time average, and
it is distinct from an averaged geometry coefficient.

The numerator is the [square of the toroidal flux-coordinate gradient
magnitude](name:square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude), and
the denominator is the square of the local magnetic-field magnitude at the
same position. The [flux-surface-averaged
ratio](name:flux_surface_averaged_ratio_of_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude_to_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude)
is obtained by applying a flux-surface average to this local quotient
itself, not by separately averaging the numerator and denominator.

items.name: parallel_electron_energy_convection_velocity
items.description:
Signed field-aligned transport velocity that multiplies electron
thermal-energy density to give the convective electron energy flux along the
local magnetic field.
items.documentation:
Parallel electron energy convection velocity parameterizes the nondiffusive
transport of electron thermal energy along the local magnetic field. It is
the field-aligned component of the [electron energy convection
velocity](name:electron_energy_convection_velocity), rather than the full
transport-velocity vector.

The defining relation is:

$$
Q_{e,W,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \mathcal{W}_e v_{e,W,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \mathcal{W}_e\,\mathbf{v}_{e,W}^{\mathrm{conv}}\cdot\mathbf{b}
$$

where $Q_{e,W,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the parallel convective
electron thermal-energy flux, $\mathcal{W}_e$ is the local electron
thermal-energy density, $v_{e,W,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this signed
convection velocity, and $\mathbf{v}_{e,W}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is its vector
parent. The unit vector $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ points along
the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

This local coefficient applies to the electron thermal-energy channel and
excludes gradient-driven energy diffusion. It multiplies energy density
rather than particle number density and need not equal the [parallel
electron bulk-flow velocity](name:parallel_electron_velocity). Its
associated flux is only the convective contribution to the [parallel
electron energy flux](name:parallel_electron_energy_flux), not the total
flux.

Sign convention: Positive when the effective electron energy convection
velocity points along the local magnetic field.

items.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_ece_channel_emission_position
items.description:
Dimensionless magnetic-surface label assigned to an electron-cyclotron
emission location, locating that emission on nested toroidal-flux surfaces.
items.documentation:
The normalized toroidal-flux coordinate at an electron-cyclotron-emission
channel's emission position is the magnetic-surface label assigned to the
location from which the channel's emission originates.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}} = \left(\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}\right)^{1/2}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ is the normalized toroidal-flux coordinate,
$\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux of the magnetic surface
passing through the emission position, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}$ is that
flux at the magnetic axis, and $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}}$ is that flux
at the equilibrium boundary.

This quantity is a point evaluation for one electron-cyclotron-emission
channel position, applying to the magnetic surface intersecting that
position. It has no sum, average, or integration over channels,
line-of-sight points, or emission locations, and it is not a cylindrical
radial distance.

It is the emission-position specialization of the [normalized toroidal flux
coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate): within the normalized
interval, it is zero at the magnetic axis and reaches one at the equilibrium
boundary. Its locus differs from the [normalized toroidal flux coordinate at
measurement
position](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_measurement_position),
which is evaluated at a measurement position rather than an
electron-cyclotron emission position.
